BJP has 4 options to resolve UGC row:How will it address upper-caste resentment while reaching out to Dalits and OBCs?
stories.summary: One thing has become clear to the BJP: on the UGC issue, the entire upper-caste (Savarna) community—namely Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, Kayasthas, and others—is not only angry, but this will also cause substantial losses in the elections. This is the reason why, during the state executive committee meeting in Lucknow on 30–31 October, state in-charge Vinod Tawde stated that the UGC controversy would be resolved before the announcement of election dates. The question is, how will it be resolved…? Sources indicate that the party is considering four options. What are these four options? What are the pros and cons of each option, and based on this, which path might the BJP choose? We will explore this in today's UP Explainer… But first, let us understand how the apprehension of electoral loss due to the UGC issue was confirmed…? The resentment of the upper castes over the UGC issue is well known, yet the BJP had assumed that it would not become an electoral issue, believing that the upper castes would eventually have to align with the BJP anyway. However, discussions regarding electoral losses began emerging across various surveys, feedback sessions, and brainstorming meetings. Subsequently, the MLC election results put the final stamp on this concern. The BJP received around 36,000 fewer votes than the SP. Moreover, slogans such as 'UGC Roll Back' and 'Withdraw the UGC rules, then talk' were written on thousands of ballot papers. Although the Election Commission rejected the votes on these ballot papers, these aggressive sentiments among educated youths made the BJP realise that this issue could disrupt calculations in the Assembly elections. Now, learn what options the BJP has to deal with this… The Supreme Court stayed the new UGC rules on 29 January 2026 and directed that the 2012 rules remain in force until further orders. That is, on an interim basis, the old system remains applicable. The government will submit in court that a balanced system can be created by making necessary amendments to the 2012 rules. Advantages: Disadvantages: Where the electoral catch lies: The BJP may get relief among its traditional upper-caste supporters, but there will remain a risk of damage to its social justice image among Dalit and backward classes. This is slightly different from the first option. Instead of strongly defending the new rules in the Supreme Court, the government will acknowledge their flaws. Seeing the apprehension of discrimination against the upper castes if the new rules are implemented, it will allow them to be struck down by the Supreme Court. Advantages: Disadvantages: Where the electoral catch lies: This could be a politically convenient route for the BJP. A direct message of relief will go to the upper castes, while the direct responsibility for scrapping the rules will not fall on the BJP government. However, the opposition may attempt to set a narrative portraying the government as anti-Dalit and anti-backward class. Under the UGC's regulatory process, the government itself withdraws or repeals the new rules. Advantages: Disadvantages: Where the electoral catch lies: This will end the anger of the upper-caste community in one stroke, but Dalit and backward castes will open a new front of protest. The SP will publicise this as an attack on the PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak — Backward, Dalit, Minority) community. This is the most balanced option. The UGC should review both the old and new rules and issue a fresh circular. This should retain provisions to prevent caste-based discrimination while ensuring there is no scope for injustice against students of any category or misuse of the rules. Advantages: Disadvantages: Where the electoral catch lies: This could be the biggest balancing act for the BJP. Through this, it can claim that it neither snatched away the rights of any section nor ignored the apprehensions of any group. However, there is no guarantee that framing the rules afresh will satisfy all social sections. Which path will the BJP choose…

stories.title: Will Azam hand over his political legacy to daughter-in-law?:Five previous attempts failed, SP may field her in 2027 Assembly elections
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party (SP) leader Azam Khan walked out of jail after 365 days, but he will still be unable to contest elections. For the first time, he may be seen campaigning for his daughter-in-law. The Samajwadi Party (SP) is almost certain to launch her political career by giving her a ticket. The seats under consideration are Rampur Sadar and Swar, both considered strongholds of the Azam family. Azam's daughter-in-law is not entering politics all of a sudden. She has made five attempts in the past, but her political entry did not materialise due to political or family reasons. Now that Azam Khan and his younger son Abdullah cannot contest elections, it has become clear that his daughter-in-law, Sidra Adeeb, may not just campaign for the family in the 2027 Assembly elections but could emerge as its candidate. On five occasions between the 2022 Assembly elections and the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, speculation intensified that Sidra Adeeb Khan would contest an election. Her name came up each time, but she had to step back because Azam Khan did not give his consent. However, the equations are different this time. First, let us look at the occasions when she tried to contest elections. 1. 2022 Assembly elections Speculation began as early as November 2021 that Sidra could contest from the Rampur Sadar seat. She had told the media, “If my father-in-law, Azam Khan, asks me to contest, I have no objection.” However, Azam Khan later decided to contest from Rampur Sadar himself while he was in jail. This ended Sidra's claim to the seat. 2. Rampur Lok Sabha by-election The Rampur Lok Sabha seat fell vacant after Azam Khan became an MLA. Sidra's name came up again during the by-election in June 2022. However, instead of getting a family member a ticket, Azam Khan fielded his close aide Asim Raja. Asim lost the election. 3. Rampur Sadar Assembly by-election Azam Khan lost his membership of the Assembly after being sentenced to three years in the hate speech case. A by-election was subsequently held for the Rampur Sadar seat in December 2022. Sidra once again came forward to contest, but Azam Khan secured the ticket for Asim Raja. Asim lost again. 4. Swar Assembly by-election After Abdullah Azam's Assembly membership was cancelled in March 2023, discussions began about fielding Sidra from the Swar seat. The matter reached Akhilesh Yadav, but once again, family members did not agree. The SP then gave the ticket to Anuradha Chauhan, who also lost the election. 5. 2024 Lok Sabha elections There was speculation that Azam Khan's elder daughter-in-law would be the party's candidate for the Lok Sabha elections. The party was preparing to give her a ticket from Rampur, but according to sources, Azam Khan and the SP leadership could not reach an agreement over the candidature. The party eventually fielded Mohibullah Nadvi. Sidra may contest from these Assembly seats... Rampur has five assembly seats. The Azam family has a strong hold over three of them: Rampur Sadar, Swar and Chamraua. If Sidra Adeeb is to contest the election, the party may consider one of these seats. However, the Rampur Sadar seat slipped out of the SP's hands in the December 2022 by-election, when the BJP's Akash Saxena won. Before that, Azam Khan himself had been elected MLA from this seat 10 times. In the 2019 by-election, his wife, Dr Tazeen Fatima, also became an MLA from the same constituency. Swar is Abdullah's traditional seat The Swar Assembly seat has traditionally been held by Azam Khan's younger son, Abdullah. Abdullah won the 2017 and 2022 Assembly elections by large margins. After his Assembly membership was cancelled, Shafiq Ahmed Ansari of Apna Dal (S), an NDA ally, won the seat in the May 2023 by-election. No member of the Azam family has contested from Chamraua No member of the Azam family has contested an election from the Chamraua seat. However, owing to Azam Khan's influence, the SP's Naseer Ahmed Khan is the MLA from this constituency. ‘People will vote for the daughter-in-law in Azam's name’ Senior journalist Siddharth Kalhans says the SP lost the Rampur seat in the 2022 by-election and will want to win it back at any cost this time. He says, “If Sidra Adeeb, Abdullah Azam or Dr Tazeen Fatima contests, they will get votes in Azam's name. Party workers will also believe that Azam Khan himself is contesting the election.” The impact will not be limited to Rampur. It could also be seen in Bareilly, Moradabad, Amroha and Pilibhit, where there is a sizeable Muslim population. Siddharth Kalhans says that if a member of the Azam family contests the election, it could also put an end to speculation about differences between the SP and Azam Khan. It would send a message to Muslim voters that Azam Khan's family is with the party.

stories.title: Electricity to be stored in water like a battery:UP and MP to jointly store 500 MW; both states to get supply for 6 months each
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh have jointly procured 500 MW of pumped storage capacity, in the country's first such unique initiative in the field of power management. Considering their different seasonal electricity requirements, the two states will store electricity through water. At present, electricity is stored only through batteries. Under the arrangement, Madhya Pradesh will use this capacity from November to April, while Uttar Pradesh will use it from May to October. This will allow a single energy storage project to be used throughout the year. It will also spare both states the additional investment required to develop separate energy storage systems. E-reverse auction process completed MP Power Management Company Limited (MPPMCL) has completed the e-reverse auction process for the agreement. This is an online bidding process for purchasing electricity, in which the company offering the lowest rate is selected. The lowest rate received in the online auction, which lasted around four hours, was ₹1.3487 crore per megawatt per year. This includes the cost of losses incurred while storing and retrieving the electricity. The company said this rate is lower than that of other such projects. Agreement to run for 40 years, benefit to come from higher electricity demand The agreement between the two states for purchasing electricity will be for 40 years. Under it, a facility to store 500 megawatts of electricity will be provided. Electricity can be stored for up to six hours, and supplied continuously for up to four hours when required. When electricity demand is low, surplus power will be used to pump water up to an elevated reservoir. When demand rises, the water will be released downhill to generate electricity. This arrangement will help address the shortage of electricity in the evening, when solar power generation declines while consumption rises. The stored electricity will be useful at such times. It will reduce the need for both states to buy electricity from elsewhere at high prices. Solar and wind power can also be utilised more effectively. Could become a model for other states as well Under this agreement, both states have taken their electricity demand periods into account. Madhya Pradesh will benefit from this facility for six months, followed by Uttar Pradesh for the next six months. This will allow the same project to be used throughout the year. This arrangement could also set an example for other states. It will help reduce the cost of electricity and ensure adequate power is available when needed. What is pumped storage? Pumped storage can be understood as a large battery for electricity. It uses water to store electricity. In simple terms, when there is surplus electricity, water is pumped uphill and stored. When electricity is needed, the water is released downhill to generate power. However, it generates slightly less electricity than the amount consumed to pump the water upwards. Typically, 70 to 85 per cent of the electricity can be recovered.

stories.title: UP women affected by violence to get ₹15 lakh compensation:Government to provide legal aid too, Yogi Cabinet changes 11-year-old policy
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government will provide financial help of up to ₹15 lakh to women and girls who are victims of serious crimes and violence. The Cabinet, chaired by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, approved the 'Rani Lakshmibai Women and Child Honour Fund Rules, 2026' on Wednesday (November 18). Under the new rules, victims will receive financial help ranging from ₹1 lakh to ₹15 lakh, depending on the seriousness of the crime. Earlier, the maximum compensation was ₹10 lakh. New system to replace 2015 scheme Until now, financial assistance was provided to women and girls who were victims under the 'Rani Lakshmibai Women's Honour Fund Rules, 2015', which came into force on 6 February 2015. The government has decided to replace these rules, which are nearly 11 years old, with the new Rules, 2026. The new system has been prepared in line with the compensation scheme of the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) and the new criminal laws. What has changed in the old and new rules Compensation amount increased- The 2015 rules provided for compensation ranging from ₹1 lakh to ₹10 lakh, depending on the severity of the crime. Under the new rules, the maximum amount has been increased to ₹15 lakh. Scope of the scheme expanded- Under the old scheme, assistance was mainly provided to women victims of offences covered under nine selected sections of the IPC. The new rules include children as well, and the scheme has been renamed the 'Rani Lakshmibai Women and Children's Honour Fund'. It has been aligned with NALSA's compensation scheme. Emphasis on immediate assistance- The new guidelines emphasise providing victims with timely financial and medical assistance. However, the process of providing immediate interim relief on the basis of a preliminary medical report and confirmation of the incident should be verified only after examining the original guidelines. Victims of which crimes will benefit? Under the new guidelines, financial assistance will be provided to women and minor girls affected by serious violence and sexual offences. The cases covered mainly include: The amount of assistance will be determined according to the severity of the crime Not every victim will receive the same amount. Financial assistance will be determined based on the seriousness of the crime, the need for treatment, and the physical and mental harm suffered by the victim. In generally serious cases, assistance will start at ₹1 lakh, while in severe cases, the amount may go up to ₹15 lakh. In addition, victims will be provided free treatment, reconstructive surgery if required, and legal assistance. The approved amount will be transferred directly to the bank account of the victim or her legal guardian.

stories.title: BJP leader’s Fortuner stolen by interior designer in Prayagraj:Made duplicate key, walked with a limp to avoid suspicion
stories.summary: An interior designer stole a BJP leader's Fortuner in Prayagraj with the help of a friend. He first got a duplicate key made and then stole the car when he got a chance. To avoid being caught, he pretended to walk with a limp while stealing the vehicle. The incident took place around midnight on October 23-24 and was captured on CCTV cameras. During the investigation, police found that the accused had taken the car from Prayagraj to Maharashtra via Rewa. They changed the original number plate and put a fake one on the vehicle. They were preparing to sell it. The Civil Lines police and Surveillance Cell arrested both accused from Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra, on Tuesday and recovered the Fortuner. On Wednesday, they brought the two accused to Prayagraj. The case is being investigated by the Civil Lines police. BJP leader's car was parked outside the hotel BJP leader and district vice-president of the OBC Morcha, Piyush Jaiswal, had his Fortuner stolen around midnight on 23-24 October. His car was parked outside the Royal Stay Inn hotel on Myor Road. When the car could not be traced despite an extensive search, he filed a case at the Civil Lines police station. Driver arrived to have the car washed, and the conspiracy was hatched According to the police, the mastermind behind the theft was Mohammad Ishtiyaq, alias Mohammad Shah. He is originally from Rasoolabad in Shivkuti, Prayagraj. He used to work in interior designing in Maharashtra. It emerged during questioning that on 9 October, BJP leader Piyush Jaiswal's driver, Mohammad Azam, had gone to Civil Lines to get the car washed. Ishtiaq arrived there during this time. The two spoke, and a plan to steal the car was made. After this, Ishtiaq, Azam and another associate together had a duplicate key made for the car. 23 October was fixed as the date for the theft. As planned, Ishtiaq first went to Maharashtra. Azam also stopped driving the car so that no one would suspect anything. On the appointed date, Ishtiaq returned to Prayagraj. The two then stole the Fortuner at night using the duplicate key. Changed His Gait to Mislead Police A notable aspect of this theft was that the incident was captured on CCTV. The footage showed the man who stole the car walking with a limp. Based on the footage, the police began investigating and tried to identify the thief. During questioning, Ishtiyaq said he had deliberately pretended to limp. His aim was to mislead the police so that the investigation would be diverted based on the identity and appearance of the man seen in the footage. Car taken from Prayagraj to Maharashtra via Rewa After stealing the car, the accused did not keep it in Prayagraj. They drove it to Rewa via Naini, Chheoki, Meja and Koraon. From there, they went to Maharashtra. On the way, they removed the car's original number plate and replaced it with a fake one. The two were then planning to sell the car in Maharashtra. The Civil Lines police and Surveillance Cell teams traced both accused during the investigation. Acting on an informer's tip-off, the police arrested Mohammad Ishtiaq and Mohammad Azam from the MIDC Ground in the Taloja police station area of the Navi Mumbai Commissionerate. The stolen Fortuner was also recovered from their possession. See the entire incident in 4 pictures He had mortgaged his Fortuner against a loan During police questioning, Ishtiyaq also explained why he committed the theft. He said he had worked in interior designing in Maharashtra. In 2020, when work came to a halt during the coronavirus pandemic, he moved to Rasoolabad in Prayagraj. He then began working while living there. During this period, he lost a substantial amount of money in share trading. Due to financial hardship and debt, he also had to mortgage his Fortuner car for ₹5 lakh. Meanwhile, he met Azam. Azam was the driver of BJP leader Piyush Jaiswal. Ishtiyaq knew that Azam had a direct connection with the car. Taking advantage of this, he planned to steal the BJP leader's Fortuner. Civil Lines police station in-charge Ramashray Yadav said the police identified the arrested accused as Mohammed Ishtiaq alias Mohammed Shah (45), a resident of Rasoolabad, Shivkuti, and Mohammed Azam (29), a resident of Bailey village under Cantt police station. The search for another accused involved in the crime is under way. Both have been sent to jail.

stories.title: Minister Nishad stages highway blockade in Maharajganj:Demands SC reservation for his community, calls Pankaj Chaudhary
stories.summary: Nishad Party national president and Cabinet Minister Sanjay Nishad took to the streets with his supporters in Maharajganj at around 4.30 p.m. on Wednesday evening, demanding Scheduled Caste (SC) reservation for the fishing community. After the conclusion of a convention and march organised at Abhinav Vidya Mandir Inter College in Uditpur, in the Farenda tehsil area, he began a sit-in on the Gorakhpur-Sonauli National Highway. This disrupted traffic on both lanes of the highway for around two hours. Long queues of vehicles formed on both sides of the road. Constitutional rights issue raised at convention A Constitutional Security Rights Mega-Conference and March was organised at Abhinav Vidya Mandir Inter College. The event raised demands for the constitutional rights of the fishing community, social justice, political representation and reservation for Scheduled Castes. At the event, Sanjay Nishad said that the fishing community had been struggling for a long time for its constitutional rights and reservation. He called on the community to take forward the fight for its rights with greater strength. Sit-in began with protesters occupying both lanes After the mega-conference ended, Sanjay Nishad reached the Gorakhpur-Sonauli National Highway with his supporters and party workers. He began a sit-in protest on both lanes of the road. The sudden blockade of the highway led to queues of vehicles forming on both sides. Commuters faced difficulties. Sanjay Nishad said he would continue sitting in protest with the workers until the government accepted their demands. Protest ended after talks with Pankaj Chaudhary After the protest continued for around two hours, Sanjay Nishad spoke to BJP state president Pankaj Chaudhary. He then decided to end the sit-in with the party workers. Traffic on the highway was restored after the sit-in ended. Following the protest over the demand for reservation, the issue of the constitutional rights of the fishing community has once again come into focus.

stories.title: ₹6 lakh paid to shooters to kill husband:Man shot in right hand; 5 arrested in Lucknow, including cop lover
stories.summary: A woman in Lucknow allegedly paid ₹6 lakh to have her husband killed. The shooters opened fire on him, but he survived the attack. Police have arrested five people, including the woman's lover, in connection with the case. According to the police, the wife, Aashi Mishra, and her lover, Nitin Rana, a Uttar Pradesh Police constable, were involved in the plan to kill her husband, Anurag Shukla. They allegedly paid ₹6 lakh for the job. Anurag was shot near Purnia Chauraha on 28 October. The bullet hit the upper part of his right arm, but he survived. Nitin Rana was among those who took the contract. Mayank Vashishtha, Shubham Sharma and Shivam Rajput were also allegedly involved. Police arrested the four men in Meerut and Aashi Mishra in Lucknow. Another accused, Mayank Rajput, is still absconding. They met at a library; affair had been ongoing since 2022 DCP North Amit Kumar Anand said Nitin Rana is a constable from the 2019 batch of the Uttar Pradesh Police and is currently posted at the Reserve Police Lines in Lucknow. He met Aashi Mishra in 2022 while preparing for competitive examinations at Maa Public Library in Kapurthala. She is a resident of Faizullaganj. The two subsequently became involved in a relationship. Aashi married Anurag Shukla, a resident of Daudnagar's Vishnu Vihar Colony, in 2025. He is employed as a sales manager at Kotak Mahindra Bank. Nitin and Ashi remained in contact even after the marriage. Nitin had also given Ashi a SIM card registered in his name, which they used to talk to each other. She plotted her husband's murder after he spoke to other women During questioning, it emerged that after the marriage, Ashi had checked her husband's mobile phone. She discovered that Anurag spoke to other women. She complained to Nitin about this. The two then planned to eliminate Anurag three months ago. Nitin contacted his acquaintance Shubham Sharma and others. A contract killing was arranged for ₹6 lakh. Some of the money was also paid in advance. Two days of reconnaissance, then gunfire in Purnia According to the DCP, the accused came to Lucknow on 26 October to carry out the conspiracy and conducted reconnaissance of Anurag's activities and the routes he used to travel. Then, at around 10:30 pm on 28 October, Mayank Vashishth and Manoj Rajput opened fire at Anurag near the gate of the Central Building at Purnia Crossing. The bullet hit his right hand. However, Anurag survived. All four accused arrested in Meerut Following the incident, the police identified the accused with the help of CCTV footage, mobile surveillance and other technical evidence. The SWAT-surveillance team of the DCP North and Aliganj police conducted a joint operation and raided a location near Maliyana railway crossing in Meerut's Transport Nagar area. Mayank Vashisht, Shubham Sharma, Shivam Rajput and constable Nitin Rana were arrested there. Ashi Mishra was apprehended in Lucknow. All the arrested accused are residents of Baghpat. According to the police, the accused threw the country-made pistol used in the incident somewhere along the way. The police are trying to recover it. Manoj Rajput, who was involved in the firing, is still absconding. Raids are being conducted to arrest him.

stories.title: UP panchayat elections delayed by 6 months:Government extends pradhans' term, approves 30 Cabinet proposals
stories.summary: Panchayat elections in Uttar Pradesh have been postponed by another six months. The state Cabinet has approved an ordinance related to the panchayats. Under the new arrangement, existing village heads will be appointed as administrators after their terms end. The tenure of the OBC Commission has also been extended. This arrangement will remain in place until the panchayat election process is completed. A total of 31 proposals were presented at the Cabinet meeting. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Suresh Khanna said that 30 proposals were approved, while one was dropped. Why have the panchayat elections been postponed? Several reasons are believed to be behind the delay. These include preparations for the 2027 Assembly elections, the OBC reservation process, the revision of voter lists and possible dissatisfaction among party workers. The Assembly elections are due in 2027. Holding panchayat elections before them could divert the government's and the party's attention from Assembly poll preparations. Local party workers could be unhappy with the distribution of tickets in the panchayat elections. This could affect the party's preparations for the Assembly elections. The panchayat election results could give an idea of the political mood in the state and influence parties' strategies for the Assembly polls. Completing the OBC reservation process is another important reason for the delay. The tenure of the OBC Commission has been extended for this purpose. Revising voter lists and completing other election preparations could also take more time. Other key Cabinet decisions Deep Tech U Hub to be set up in Noida, ₹281.03 crore approved The Cabinet has approved ₹281.03 crore for setting up a Deep Tech U Hub at IIT Kanpur's Noida campus. A budget of ₹100 crore will be provided for the project in the current financial year. The Central Government will not provide any funds for it. The construction work is expected to be completed within 24 months. Suresh Khanna said the project aims to promote new ideas, support start-ups and create more job opportunities in the state. Land in Agra to be given to Sports Department for stadium The Cabinet has approved the transfer of land in Uganpura gram panchayat in the Bah area of Agra to the Sports Department for building a stadium. The land is currently registered in the name of the Youth Department. The stadium will provide local and upcoming players with a place to showcase their talent. Cooperative college to be built in Rahman Kheda The Cabinet has approved the allocation of 4.51 hectares of land in Rahman Kheda, Lucknow, to an institution under the Cooperation Department. A cooperative college will be built on the land to promote education, research and training in this field. The institution will also offer courses related to artificial intelligence (AI). A hostel and a hall with a capacity of 1,000 people will also be built there. The aim is to prepare skilled professionals in the field of cooperation. Changes to rules related to waqf properties The Cabinet has approved changes to the rules related to waqf properties. This will help put the arrangements linked to the Ummeed portal in place. Land arrangements for Kashi Vishwanath Corridor The Cabinet has also approved a proposal related to land arrangements for the Kashi Vishwanath Corridor. Other key decisions The Cabinet has approved a proposal to provide compensation to farmers affected by the Jewar Airport project. Proposals to promote the semiconductor and deep-tech sectors in the state have also been approved. These aim to attract investment and create jobs in new technology fields. A proposal related to the operation of 102 and 108 ambulance services has been approved. A logistics cluster will be developed near the Purvanchal Expressway. It will have facilities for storing and transporting goods. The Cabinet has approved a residential project on the site of the old police lines in Agra. A yoga centre will be built in Baghpat. Changes to the rules of the Women and Child Honour Fund have been approved. The Cabinet has approved a proposal to take technical help from IIT-ISM Dhanbad for mining-related work.

stories.title: Fire breaks out in Lucknow slums:Plastic items fuel blaze, 10 fire engines deployed to control it
stories.summary: A massive fire broke out in the slums of Aishbagh, under the Bazar Khala police station area in Lucknow, at around 4 pm on Wednesday. Thick black smoke from the fire could be seen from nearly 4 km away. After seeing smoke rising from the area, people alerted the fire brigade. The fire spread quickly, causing panic among residents. Four fire engines reached the spot and started efforts to control the flames. The fire is reportedly flaring up again and again because a large amount of plastic items is stored in the slums. Check out pictures below : Area thrown into chaos by raging flames According to eyewitnesses, smoke began rising from the shanties at around 4 p.m. People initially tried to put out the fire, but the flames began spreading rapidly. The fire brigade was then alerted. Four fire engines at the scene As soon as the information was received, four fire engines reached the spot. Firefighters are working to bring the blaze under control. The presence of plastic materials is making it difficult to extinguish the fire, and the flames are repeatedly intensifying.

stories.summary: The BJP has formed a five-member state disciplinary committee in Uttar Pradesh to maintain discipline within the organisation. According to official party information, the committee will hear and investigate complaints of indiscipline against the party's elected representatives, office-bearers and workers. Key names included in the committee The new disciplinary committee formed by the BJP includes five senior organisational leaders as members: How will this committee function? Under the party's rules, if a complaint of indiscipline or anti-party activities is received against any elected representative, office-bearer or worker, the committee will hear the case. After hearing the parties concerned, the committee will prepare its inquiry report, on the basis of which a final decision will be taken on further action against the leader or worker found guilty.

stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav received a special welcome in Kudaghat, Gorakhpur. A poster showing his picture was hung from a crane with the message, "Akhilesh Yadav is Gen Z's favourite." A huge garland was also hung between two cranes to welcome the Samajwadi Party chief. As soon as his PDA Rath reached the spot, Akhilesh asked the driver to stop the bus. The area echoed with slogans as party workers cheered for him. Seeing the excitement among his supporters, Akhilesh climbed onto the roof of the bus and waved at the crowd. Bus stopped to receive workers' welcome Akhilesh Yadav's roadshow passed through the Gorakhpur City, Gorakhpur Rural and Chauri Chaura assembly constituencies. He also addressed a public meeting in Chauri Chaura. Akhilesh Yadav attended a tribute meeting in Devkahi held on the 10th death anniversary of former BJP leader Vinay Kumar Singh Binnu. He also unveiled a statue of martyr Bandhu Singh there.

stories.title: 600 couples to get married under government scheme in Varanasi:Brides to receive ₹64,000 each; events to be held across all blocks
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government will organise mass marriage ceremonies for 600 couples across all eight development blocks of Varanasi under the Chief Minister's Mass Marriage Scheme. The ceremonies will be held from November 21 to the first week of December. Under the scheme, ₹64,000 will be transferred directly to the bank account of each bride. The newly married couples will also receive household items to help them start their new lives. District Social Welfare Officer Girish Chandra Dubey said preparations had been completed for the ceremonies. The programme will be held in Sevapuri, Harhua, Arajiline, Pindra, Baragaon, Cholapur, Kashi Vidyapeeth and Chiraigaon blocks. Block-wise marriage schedule Sevapuri: November 21 – 80 couples Harhua: November 25 – 80 couples Arajiline: November 26 – 80 couples Pindra: November 26 – 80 couples Baragaon: November 26 – 80 couples Cholapur: November 29 – 80 couples Kashi Vidyapeeth: December 3 – 30 couples Chiraigaon: First week of December – 90 couples What will brides receive? Apart from the ₹64,000 grant, each couple will receive household items, including five sarees, a steel dinner set, a pressure cooker, a trolley bag, an iron, a ceiling fan, a blanket and a mattress. The items will help the couples set up their homes. The scheme aims to support families who cannot afford the expenses of their daughters' marriages.

stories.title: 23 rare turtles found in 13 bags at Varanasi station:2 women carrying children arrested for smuggling them from Sultanpur to West Bengal
stories.summary: A joint team of the Government Railway Police (GRP), Railway Protection Force (RPF) and Central Intelligence Bureau (CIB) recovered 23 rare turtles from Banaras railway station. The turtles were packed in 13 bags and bundles. Two women travelling with their children were detained in connection with the case. The incident took place on Tuesday night when the women were found sitting in the station's closed parking area near the second entrance. They had two children with them, one around 1.5 years old and the other around three years old. Several bags and bundles were kept beside them. According to RPF post in-charge Rajesh, police teams were patrolling the station due to the festive season when they noticed the women. When asked about their names and addresses, they did not give any information. The team became suspicious and took them to the GRP outpost. During a search of their bags, the team found 23 rare turtles. According to the Forest Department, the turtles were being taken from Sultanpur to West Bengal through Varanasi. Their estimated market value is more than ₹3 lakh. They had arrived in Banaras by bus from Sultanpur The RPF in-charge said that when the women's bags were searched, 23 rare tortoises of different sizes were found. All of them had been packed into 13 bags and bundles. The women, who were arrested, identified themselves as Manisha, a resident of Pakri under Hanumanganj police station in Sultanpur district, and Sapna, a resident of Pakri under Hanumanganj police station in Sultanpur district. Both women also have children, whom they were going to take along while travelling. Sold in West Bengal for more than ₹3 lakh Regional Forest Officer Rajkumar Gautam, who reached the spot after receiving information, said 23 turtles had been seized at Varanasi's Banaras Junction. All these turtles were being prepared for transportation from Sultanpur to West Bengal via Varanasi. He said, "We reached here after receiving information from police officers." These are all rare turtles. They are taken to West Bengal and sold at high prices. Their international value is more than ₹3 lakh.

stories.title: Akhilesh's Gorakhpur roadshow grabs attention:2-foot dancers, selfie crowds and laptop-waving supporters steal the show
stories.summary: From a two-foot-tall SP worker surrounded by people wanting selfies to supporters dancing to drum beats and waving laptops while riding horses, Akhilesh Yadav's Gorakhpur roadshow on Wednesday saw people come up with different ways to grab attention. A large crowd gathered to welcome the Samajwadi Party chief. Riding on the PDA Rath, Akhilesh received a warm welcome at several places, while SP flags, hoardings and cutouts covered the streets. 2-foot-tall SP worker becomes selfie attraction Chand Babu, a two-foot-tall Samajwadi Party worker from Bhadohi, reached Gorakhpur airport to welcome Akhilesh. As soon as people spotted him, they gathered around to shake hands and click selfies. The crowd grew so large that he eventually had to leave the spot. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, Chand Babu said he had travelled around 266 km from Bhadohi to welcome the party chief. Calling himself the party's "smallest soldier", he said he followed every order given by Akhilesh. He also said his family had followed socialist ideas for generations. "My grandfather and great-grandfather were socialists, and we will remain so throughout our lives. This time, Akhilesh Yadav will become the Chief Minister. The entire public is with him," he said. Supporters wave laptops and welcome Akhilesh with a huge garland Supporters came up with other ways to show their excitement. One person had Akhilesh's name written on his body, while another arrived on a horse and waved a laptop in the air. Shubham also wore a T-shirt with "2027 ke Sattadhish" written on it. At Kudaghat crossing, two cranes lifted a huge garland to welcome Akhilesh. The SP chief had his PDA Rath stopped as supporters raised slogans. Seeing their enthusiasm, he climbed onto the roof of the bus and waved at the crowd. Red-cap supporter dances to drum beats Another young supporter grabbed attention by dancing on the road. Wearing a red cap with "Yuvjan Sabha" written on it, he started dancing as soon as the drums began playing. He raised his hands and moved to the beats with full energy. People stopped to watch and cheer him, while other SP supporters also joined in. Two-foot-tall Shubham surprises Akhilesh with his dance Shubham, another two-foot-tall dancer, also became a talking point during the roadshow. Wearing a T-shirt with Akhilesh Yadav's picture on it, he danced enthusiastically on the road. His energetic moves made people stop and clap. Even Akhilesh was surprised by his performance. Akhilesh holds first Gorakhpur roadshow since 2024 polls This was Akhilesh's first visit to Gorakhpur for a political programme since the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. His roadshow passed through Gorakhpur City, Gorakhpur Rural and Chauri Chaura assembly constituencies. Later, addressing a public meeting in Chauri Chaura, Akhilesh paid tribute to Babu Bandhu Singh and the martyrs of the Chauri Chaura incident. He also thanked people for the support they showed during the roadshow.

stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath launched a joint training programme of the National Security Guard (NSG) and Uttar Pradesh Police in Lucknow on Wednesday. During the programme, NSG commandos conducted a mock drill in front of the Chief Minister. They showed how they would respond to a terrorist attack inside a building. The commandos arrived by helicopter and used ropes to reach the building's roof. They then entered through the windows and took down the terrorists one by one. They also rescued the hostages safely. An NSG dog also took part in the operation and helped the commandos. After the drill, the dog, Johnny, presented a bouquet to CM Yogi and saluted him. The aim of the joint training programme is to improve coordination between the NSG and Uttar Pradesh Police. Police personnel will be trained to handle situations such as terrorist attacks. stories.title: Nephew kills gym trainer in Agra:Repeatedly attacks his face with a stone, leaving his jaw and eyes disfigured
stories.summary: A gym trainer was killed by his brother and nephew in Agra on Tuesday. On Wednesday, a video linked to the murder emerged. It shows the nephew repeatedly striking the gym trainer on the head with a stone. The accused kept hitting the gym trainer until his eyes and jaw were dislodged. His teeth broke and were scattered on the road. After the murder, the accused tried to throw the gym trainer, covered in blood, into a drain. When people raised an alarm, the accused fled. New Agra police station has registered a case against the accused. First, read the full case Dispute over 120 square yards of land Shahid, alias Guddu Pehalwan, a 49-year-old resident of Suresh Nagar, was a gym trainer. He was currently running a grocery shop near his home. He was one of four brothers. Shahid's son Ajaan said there was 120 square yards of land behind their house. His father had an ongoing dispute over the land with his elder brother, Afsar alias Lala, and younger brother, Bunty Qureshi. "We had already won the case in court. Despite this, both brothers continued to harass us," he said. On Monday morning, uncle Afsar and uncle Bunty reached the land with other people. The accused arrived carrying a door and a door frame. They began construction on the land. My father, Shahid, objected. When the accused refused to stop, my father went to New Agra police station. The police then reached the spot and stopped the construction. At 8:30 a.m. on Tuesday, another dispute broke out over the land. The women from both sides confronted each other. As the dispute escalated, Shahid left to lodge a complaint at the police station. His friend Dilshad was with him on the scooter. Surrounded 150 metres from home, killed in a stone attack Shahid had reached a point about 150 metres from his home when the accused surrounded both of them on the way. The accused pulled Shahid off his scooter and knocked him to the ground. They kicked and punched him and tried to drag him into a drain. Shahid then confronted the accused. Meanwhile, Mehtab and Aftab, the two sons of Afsar alias Lala, attacked Shahid with a stone. Shahid fell on the road as soon as the stone hit him. Mehtab then picked up a large stone from the road and began repeatedly striking Shahid's face. The accused struck him four times with the stone in 17 seconds. Shahid's jaw was fractured, his eyes protruded and his broken teeth were scattered across the road. When people raised an alarm, the accused fled the scene. Shahid's friend ran home and informed his family. His family took Shahid, who was covered in blood, to the police station. From there, they first took him to the district hospital and then to a private hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Now read what the video shows In the 17-second video, the accused, Guddu Pehalwan, is seen attacking the victim with a stone four times. People are seen standing and shouting, trying to stop him. But he did not stop. The people continued standing and recording the video, but no one had the courage to stop the accused. After the murder, the accused fled the scene. Shahid is survived by three sons, Azaan, Faiz and Zaid, and a daughter. His father, Raheesh, died in 2016. Meanwhile, Nazneen lost consciousness after her husband was murdered. ACP Hariparvat Bajrang Prasad said an FIR had been registered on the complaint of Shahid's friend, Dilshad. A team has been deployed to arrest the accused.

stories.title: Akhilesh says government is scared, shuts down internet:Holds 20-km roadshow in Gorakhpur, says city feels like Europe
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party national president Akhilesh Yadav arrived in Gorakhpur on Wednesday for his first political programme in the city since the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. He held a roadshow on the PDA Rath, passing through Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's stronghold and receiving a warm welcome from supporters at several places. The roadshow passed through Gorakhpur City, Gorakhpur Rural and Chauri Chaura Assembly constituencies. The BJP and its allies held power in all three seats. Akhilesh also addressed a public meeting in Chauri Chaura. A large number of supporters gathered to see him. Amrita Yadav, a student who attended the roadshow, said she was a big fan of Akhilesh and liked everything he said. She added that she was not old enough to vote yet, but would support her parents when they cast their votes. She also raised slogans in support of the SP chief. Another supporter, Muskan Yadav, said she had come to see Akhilesh and hoped the Samajwadi Party would form the government in 2027. She said a change in government would bring many changes and that she expected a new direction under Akhilesh's leadership. Taking a dig at the current government, she said it had done nothing during its term. Roadshow held on PDA chariot The Samajwadi PDA chariot had arrived in Gorakhpur on Tuesday night. Akhilesh boarded it at Gorakhpur airport at 12 noon on Wednesday and left for Devkahi. On the way, he passed through AIIMS, Gurung Tiraha in Kudaghat, the Engineering University and Sooba Bazaar. Supporters welcomed him at several places. The chariot began its journey in the Gorakhpur City Assembly constituency before entering Gorakhpur Rural and Chauri Chaura. Akhilesh greeted people from inside the chariot and also stepped out to acknowledge their welcome. Akhilesh pays tribute to martyrs In Devkahi, Akhilesh attended a programme marking the 10th death anniversary of former BJP leader Vinay Kumar Singh Binnu. He also unveiled a statue of martyr Bandhu Singh and paid tribute to him and the martyrs of the Chauri Chaura incident. Addressing the gathering, Akhilesh thanked people for the support they had shown during the roadshow. At the end of his speech, he took a dig at the government over the internet shutdown, saying it was scared and had therefore stopped internet services. Visit aimed at reaching upper-caste voters Akhilesh's visit also focused on upper-caste voters, particularly Kshatriya and Brahmin communities. He attended the programme held on the death anniversary of former BJP leader Binnu Singh. Binnu Singh's brother, Tappu Singh, had received around 30,000 votes as an independent candidate in the 2022 Assembly elections. The Samajwadi Party was preparing to bring him into the party and hoped to gain support among Kshatriya voters in Chauri Chaura and nearby constituencies. Akhilesh also visited Tiwari Hata, the residence of Samajwadi Party national secretary Vinay Shankar Tiwari, son of former minister Harishankar Tiwari, in Dharamshala Bazaar. He stayed there for around 30 minutes. The visit was seen as an attempt to reach out to Brahmin voters. Visit also seen as a challenge to Nishad Party Akhilesh's programme in Chauri Chaura was also seen as a political challenge to the Nishad Party. Its national president Dr Sanjay Nishad's younger son, Er. Sarwan Nishad, represented the constituency and had won the seat on a BJP ticket. The Samajwadi Party aimed to strengthen its position in the constituency by bringing Tappu Singh into its fold. Through the programme, it also sought to expand its support in nearby Assembly constituencies.

stories.title: 'Akhilesh can neither attend nor organise a Katha':Dhirendra Shastri says he would hold one if he ever develops faith
stories.summary: Pandit Dhirendra Shastri took a swipe at Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav in Pratapgarh. He said, "He is a very good person; we are not his opponents. We would only say that he should also come and listen to the discourse. In any case, such a time will not come when he can listen to or organise our discourse. But if faith ever awakens within him, we will conduct a discourse for him without hesitation." In Kunda, MLA Raghuraj Pratap Singh (Raja Bhaiya) is organising a Ram Katha by Bageshwar Dham seer Dhirendra Shastri. After completing the discourse on the first day, Tuesday, Dhirendra Shastri appeared before the media and answered their questions. On his comment about Krishna, he said, "My statement was given a political colour. Confusion was spread. Krishna is in our very name." Today, Wednesday, is the second day of the Ram Katha. Earlier in the morning, Dhirendra Shastri went to bathe in the Ganga. He then offered prayers at Haudeshwar Nath Temple. Raja Bhaiya is the patron of this temple. Mahant Raju Das of Hanumangarhi was present with him. Read Pt Dhirendra Shastri's question-and-answer session with the media Question: Akhilesh Yadav has been attacking you more aggressively. Why is that? Answer: There must be something about us that is causing this. As for the question of whether my religious discourse is cheap or expensive, understand that we are not selling a commodity; religion is not a business. If it were a business, it would be cheap. Religion is a matter of faith. There are many wealthy people who want to organise my religious discourse. If they approach us as though they are buying the discourse, we will not go; if they do it out of faith, we will go along just the same. Question: Several Opposition leaders besides the Samajwadi Party chief are also upset with you. What do you have to say? Answer: We do not offer lengthy explanations because we have set out to do our work, so it is natural that all kinds of things will be said. Under the Constitution, religious discourses cannot be stopped. If they are stopped, prayers at mosques will also be stopped. Prayers in churches will also be stopped. If that happens, the system will be disrupted. Hindus are awakening, followers of Sanatan Dharma are awakening and responding assertively. Question: You are holding religious discourses in Uttar Pradesh and benefiting politicians? Answer: Those who listen to, deliver and organise a discourse benefit from it. Not only them, but sound-system providers, television channels and news organisations also benefit from it. As for the fact that this is an election year, that is not the case; we hold discourses throughout the five-year term. We conduct these discourses not for elections, but for Sanatan Dharma. Question: You said that there is a need for another Partition. Why? Answer: There has not yet been a complete Partition. Some people had been left behind because they were afraid in India. It is such a safe country, yet if they are still afraid, they should leave. Some Hindus want to come from Pakistan; they should be allowed to come. The Hindus who have already come to India should be granted citizenship here. This is my view: if someone wants a complete Partition, it should happen. Question: Did you divide Ram and Krishna in your discourse? Answer: It is impossible to understand a 30-second excerpt from a three-hour discourse after it has been edited. People cut out that portion and circulated it in that form. The confusion will disappear once you listen to the entire discourse. It was given a political colour. It had nothing to do with denigrating God in any way. After all, how could someone narrating the discourse denigrate Krishna-especially someone who has Krishna in his own name? What happened during the discourse on the first day? Read on In fact, on 5 November, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav had demanded the cancellation of Dhirendra Shastri's discourses scheduled to be held in Pratapgarh, Gonda, Jhansi, Lucknow and Agra.

stories.title: Chandrashekhar's ex-girlfriend from Indore to contest against him:Accused him of sexual exploitation; performed a ritual at Baglamukhi Temple
stories.summary: Dr Rohini Ghavari, the former girlfriend of Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad who accused him of sexual exploitation, arrived in Nalkheda in Agar-Malwa on Tuesday night. She visited the Maa Baglamukhi Temple and performed a havan ritual. Rohini said she had come to seek the goddess's blessings for victory in her court case and justice. She also said she would contest the election from the Hastinapur Assembly seat against Chandrashekhar Azad. However, she has not yet clarified whether she will contest on a political party's ticket or as an independent candidate. Also met Digvijaya Singh and Kailash Vijayvargiya Rohini returned to India from Switzerland around eight months ago. Since then, she has met former Chief Ministers Digvijaya Singh and Kamal Nath, as well as state minister Kailash Vijayvargiya, in Delhi and Bhopal. These meetings sparked speculation about her possible entry into politics. Who is Rohini Ghavari, and what is the dispute with Chandrashekhar? Dr Rohini Ghavari is from Indore. Under the Madhya Pradesh government's fellowship scheme, she got an opportunity to study in Switzerland. She completed her PhD there. During this period, she met Bhim Army founder Chandrashekhar Azad. Rohini alleges that Chandrashekhar concealed the fact that he was married, promised to marry her and sexually exploited her. According to her, Chandrashekhar began distancing himself from her after he was elected MP from Nagina. Rohini had also lodged a complaint with the Women's Commission in this matter. Meanwhile, Chandrashekhar and his supporters had an FIR registered against Rohini. Rohini has also been consistently voicing her views against Chandrashekhar on social media. Indications of entering politics While studying in Switzerland, Rohini also founded an NGO called 'Janpower'. After returning to India, her meetings with political leaders and now her announcement that she will contest the election have intensified speculation about her political future.

stories.title: Azam walks out of jail, son says ‘Tiger is back':Spends a year behind bars; 600 supporters gather outside Dasna jail
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan walked out of jail exactly a year after being sent behind bars. As soon as he saw Azam, his son Adeeb said, “The tiger is back. Today is like Eid for us.” As soon as Azam came out of jail, supporters and media personnel surrounded him. Azam said, “I have always said the same thing. A Muslim built a temple of education, and this is his punishment.” He then left for his home in Rampur in a Scorpio SUV. More than 600 supporters were present outside the jail. They raised slogans of “Long live Azam Khan”. Azam was sent to Rampur jail on November 17, 2025, in a case related to two PAN cards. He thus spent an entire year behind bars. Earlier, at around 4.30 pm on Wednesday, the release order for Azam reached Dasna jail in Ghaziabad. He was released after the paperwork was completed. It may be recalled that Azam had also walked out of Rampur jail on October 31, but the Enforcement Directorate (ED) arrested him immediately. He had been lodged in Dasna jail since then. Earlier on Wednesday morning, the ED approached the Supreme Court challenging Azam's interim bail. The agency sought an urgent hearing in the case. The judge reprimanded the ED, saying, “What is the hurry? Let Azam remain out on bail. It is not the end of the world.” Azam's case to be heard again in Supreme Court on Thursday The Enforcement Directorate (ED) approached the Supreme Court on Wednesday morning challenging Azam's interim bail. It sought an immediate hearing in the case. However, the court has scheduled the hearing for Thursday (November 19). The court may either overturn the Allahabad High Court's order or uphold it. If the High Court's order is overturned, Azam may have to return to jail. Meanwhile, the Vigilance Department has registered an FIR against Azam in Lucknow in connection with the Haj House case. He could also be arrested in this case. However, the department will need approval from the state government before making the arrest. Akhilesh says the government wronged Azam Khan and his family Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav expressed happiness after Azam Khan was granted interim bail. He said Azam Khan had received justice from the court. The government had wronged Azam Khan and his family for several years. Akhilesh said, "We have been saying from the first day that the cases registered against Azam Khan are false and that the government's action is wrong. The government's intentions are not right. Several things have come to light today through the court's observations. We have complete faith that justice will be delivered by the court." Minister Jaiveer Singh says being granted bail and being cleared of the charges are two different things Uttar Pradesh government minister Jaiveer Singh said the government respects the court's order. Under the constitutional system, courts and other institutions independently take decisions within their respective powers. When the court has granted bail, what comment can the government make on it? The order will be followed. The minister said that being granted bail does not mean being cleared of the charges. The two are different matters. The cases will now be heard in court. The final decision will come only after the trial is completed. Could Azam's release cause trouble for the BJP? Read ... Azam Khan has been sentenced to 10 years in the PAN card case, while Abdullah Azam has been sentenced in the PAN card and fake birth certificate cases. Both have also been disqualified as members of the Legislative Assembly. Under Section 8(3) of the Representation of the People Act, a person sentenced to two years or more cannot contest elections for six years after completing the sentence. This disqualification is not removed merely by being granted bail. A stay on the sentence from a higher court is necessary to contest an election. However, Azam's release before the 2027 Assembly election could prove significant for the Samajwadi Party. Understand its political impact in 3 points... 1. He will become the SP's star campaigner Despite being unable to contest elections, Azam Khan can campaign for the SP. His speeches in Muslim-dominated seats in western Uttar Pradesh are expected to boost the morale of party workers. 2. Countering Owaisi's challenge Azam's return may help the Samajwadi Party prevent Muslim votes from splitting. The party will regain its old and outspoken face to take on the challenge posed by Asaduddin Owaisi's AIMIM. 3. Organisation to be strengthened in western UP Azam has had influence in western UP, including the Rampur and Moradabad divisions. His return may help fill the vacuum in the party's minority leadership created by his absence. Akhilesh may assign him responsibility for coordinating the party's seats in western UP. What will be the BJP's next move? After Azam's release, the BJP may target the Samajwadi Party on law and order and corruption issues. According to senior journalist Jaigam Murtaza, Azam's release could reactivate the SP's local organisation in Rampur and the surrounding districts. This could affect the political contest in the 2027 election.

stories.title: Who was Binnu Singh? Akhilesh to visit and pay tribute:He campaigned against Mahant Avaidyanath and contested against Union minister's father
stories.summary: SP chief Akhilesh Yadav is visiting Gorakhpur today, 18 November, on his first political tour of the district in connection with the 2027 Assembly elections. He will pay tribute to late Vinay Kumar Singh 'Binnu' on his 10th death anniversary at Devkahi in the Chauri Chaura Assembly constituency. At the same event, Ajay Kumar Singh, Binnu Singh's brother, will be inducted into the SP. Ten years have passed since Binnu Singh's death, but he is once again in the spotlight because of the SP chief's programme. Binnu Singh had been a combative politician from the outset. Binnu Singh, who began his political career in student politics, once campaigned against Yogi Adityanath's guru, Mahant Avedyanath, in a Lok Sabha election. In the 1990s, he contested an Assembly election against late Om Prakash Paswan. Om Prakash's elder son, Kamlesh Paswan, is currently a minister in the Union government. Entered student politics and secured a victory Binnu Singh was regarded as a dynamic leader from his youth. In the 1980s, he entered the fray in the student union election at Gorakhpur University and succeeded in winning. In the 1989 election, he joined the Janata Dal. At the time, the Janata Dal had given Rampal Singh a Lok Sabha ticket, while the BJP had supported him. Binnu Singh was very close to Rampal Singh. During this election, he openly campaigned against Mahant Avaidyanath, who was contesting on the Hindu Mahasabha banner. However, Mahant Avaidyanath succeeded in winning the election. After this, Binnu Singh joined the BJP. In the 1993 election, the BJP gave him a ticket from Maniram. The seat was considered Mahant Avaidyanath's traditional constituency. Late Om Prakash Paswan had been elected BJP MLA from here in 1991. In 1993, he was again staking his claim. However, Om Prakash Paswan contested this election as an independent. The BJP fielded Binnu Singh against him. However, late Om Prakash Paswan won the election by a huge margin. He received more than 59% of the votes. Janata Dal's Shambhu Sharan, who came second, received 18.89% of the votes, while Binnu Singh received only 13.34%. Binnu Remained Active in the BJP After this election, he remained continuously active in the BJP. He was considered very close to senior BJP leader Kalraj Mishra. Meanwhile, his family also became associated with Gorakhnath Temple. Ajay Kumar Singh Tappu, Binnu Singh's brother, told a media organisation that his family had donated land and provided other assistance for Gorakhnath Temple and Madan Mohan Malaviya University of Technology (MMUT). His family is said to be descended from martyr Bandhu Singh. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath also regularly speaks about martyr Bandhu Singh on various platforms. Brother Sought BJP Ticket; Entered Fray as Independent After Being Denied Ajay Kumar Singh Tappu is Binnu Singh's younger brother. He is a contractor by profession. He also runs a hotel in Mohaddipur. He has educational institutions as well. Binnu Singh died in November 2016. After his death, Tappu Singh gradually became active in politics. In 2022, he sought the BJP ticket but was not given one. Tappu Singh then contested the election as an independent. Following this, he was expelled from the party. Contesting as an independent, Tappu Singh received around 30,000 votes. He has decided to contest the election this time as well. When there appeared to be no possibility of getting a BJP ticket, he approached the Samajwadi Party. The SP is expected to field Tappu Singh from Chauri Chaura.

stories.title: 8 special trains to run from Lucknow to- Mumbai:6 new services introduced, trips of 2 trains increased
stories.summary: North Eastern Railway has decided to operate eight special trains in view of the rising rush on trains after Diwali and Chhath. One additional trip each has been added to two trains already in operation, while six new special trains will be run. They will operate between 18 and 22 November. This will provide relief to passengers travelling from Gorakhpur, Chhapra and Mau to Delhi, Mumbai and Udhna. One additional trip each added to two trains One additional trip of the Lokmanya Tilak Terminus-Gorakhpur Special (01041/01042) will operate. Train number 01041 will depart from Lokmanya Tilak Terminus on 19 November. On the return journey, train number 01042 will depart from Gorakhpur on 21 November. Similarly, one additional trip of the Hadapsar-Gorakhpur Special (01457/01458) has also been scheduled. Train number 01457 will depart from Hadapsar on 20 November, while train number 01458 will depart from Gorakhpur on 22 November on the return journey. Special trains also for Chhapra and Delhi In addition, the Chhapra-Anand Vihar Terminal Special (05057/05058) and Gorakhpur-Delhi Special (05051/05052) will operate on 19 and 20 November. According to the railway, trains are experiencing additional crowding as passengers return after the festival. Special trains have therefore been arranged.

stories.title: Fog blankets UP, speed limits reduced on expressways:Bareilly records lowest temperature; 'Akvan' storm to intensify cold and fog
stories.summary: Snowfall in the hills has intensified the cold in Uttar Pradesh. Dense fog is affecting the state during the morning and night hours. Visibility has dropped so low that objects beyond 10 metres are barely visible on roads. Due to the fog, speed limits have been reduced on expressways. The speed limits on the Agra-Lucknow, Purvanchal, Bundelkhand, Gorakhpur Link and Ganga Expressways have been set between 50 and 80 kmph. Cars will not be allowed to exceed 80 kmph, buses 60 kmph and goods vehicles such as trucks 50 kmph. On Wednesday morning, fog covered 15 cities, including Gorakhpur, Deoria, Jaunpur, Mau and Kushinagar. Roads remained deserted. Over the past 24 hours, night temperatures have dropped to around 10°C, while temperatures in 20 districts fell below 15°C. Bareilly was the coldest city, recording 11.1°C. Atul Kumar Singh, a meteorologist in Lucknow, said the impact of Cyclone 'Akvan', which formed over the Bay of Bengal, is now moving from south to north. As a result, cloud cover, cold conditions and fog are expected to intensify over the next 24 hours. Bay of Bengal storm to change the weather According to the meteorologist, temperatures may remain normal or below normal for the next two to three days. After that, the direction of the winds is likely to change under the influence of Cyclonic Storm 'Akwan', which has formed in the Bay of Bengal. This could lead to a rise of 2 to 3 degrees Celsius in temperatures. For now, the chill will intensify in the morning and at night, while sunshine during the day will keep the weather relatively pleasant. Now find out what the weather will be like over the next 2 days What is the Air Quality Index (AQI)? It is a score that indicates air quality and helps us understand whether the air around us is clean or polluted. The AQI measures the levels of pollutants present in the air. stories.title: BJP leadership accepts lapse over UGC issue:Party chalks out election strategy in Mathura; youth and women to be key focus
stories.summary: Discontent over the UGC's new regulations was raised at the BJP's two-day meeting in Mathura. The central leadership said the government had also acknowledged that there had been some lapses in drafting the regulations. These would be rectified. The meeting was told that the UGC matter is currently pending before the Supreme Court. However, the government will organise the entire process. The central leadership assured the meeting that no law or regulation would be implemented that could ruin anyone's future or cause injustice to anyone. In September, protests were held at several places in Uttar Pradesh over the UGC's new regulations. Upper-caste groups, in particular, had targeted the BJP government. The protesters were put in touch with Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak. The agitation ended only after they were assured that their demands would be conveyed to the central government. The BJP fears that upper-caste voters may shift towards the Samajwadi Party in the 2027 Assembly election. For now, the central leadership has made it clear that the government does not intend to discriminate against any section. Any shortcomings in the rules will be addressed so that everyone's interests can be taken into account. Read about the issues on which the BJP has prepared a strategy to corner opposition parties.... On 16 and 17 November, the BJP held a two-day state planning meeting at the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay Research Centre in Parakham, Mathura. This was national president Nitin Nabin's fifth visit to Uttar Pradesh. He had earlier visited the western, Awadh, Kashi and Gorakhpur regions. Will remind young voters of the Samajwadi Party government's failures According to the BJP leaders who attended the meeting, young people who are preparing to vote for the first or second time today were very young during the Samajwadi Party government before 2017. They have seen only BJP rule at the Centre since 2014 and in the state since 2017. The party believes it is important to inform these new voters about the law-and-order situation, recruitment controversies, the Jawaharb​​agh incident and issues related to women's safety during the earlier period. Only 25% of young people who received tablets were voters Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath shared an important statistic about the electoral roll at the meeting. He said tablets had been distributed in Lucknow to young people above the age of 18 under the Swami Vivekananda Youth Empowerment Scheme. When they were asked how many of them were voters, only 25% of the young people raised their hands. Chief Minister Yogi directed office-bearers to ensure that 100% of the young population is enrolled in the electoral roll. He said the electoral roll for the panchayat elections should be compared with the Assembly electoral roll so that no eligible voter is left out. Speculation Over Organisation, Leadership and Tickets Put to Rest BJP national president Nitin Nabin made it clear at the meeting that there is no crisis whatsoever regarding the organisation, leadership or government in the state, while emphasising that the organisation is paramount. The public has faith in the work of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. 'Nationalism' and new slogans to counter caste politics Nitin Naveen told party workers, "Opposition parties are trying to divide society along caste lines, but the youth and women must be kept united around the issue of nationalism rather than caste. The SP, BSP, Congress and the third front-none of them is an ally, so an aggressive strategy will have to be adopted towards all of them." Suggestions for slogans were also sought from office-bearers at the meeting to give momentum to the election campaign. Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak suggested around a dozen slogans, with 'Uttar Pradesh Will Answer' emerging as the most prominent. MLC Santosh Singh and Parliamentary Affairs Minister Suresh Khanna also presented election slogans. A special team comprising former and current office-bearers will now be formed to prepare a roadmap for taking these issues and campaigns to the ground. The meeting discussed the party's action plan for the next three months. It also covered strengthening the organisation, increasing party activities and improving coordination with the NDA's allies. Tribute Also Paid to Ashok Singhal The meeting began with the garlanding of Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay's statue. This was followed by a floral tribute to the portrait of late Ashok Singhal, former international president of the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP), on his death anniversary. National General Secretary (Organisation) BL Santosh, National General Secretary Vinod Tawde, Smriti Irani and Harish Dwivedi were present at the meeting. In addition, more than 50 senior leaders, including Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Deputy Chief Ministers Keshav Prasad Maurya and Brajesh Pathak, attended.
