stories.title: Akhilesh has consulted astrologers for auspicious timings before:Asked a 'Panditji' before Ram Lalla's darshan; now turns to astrology to become CM again
stories.summary: Astrology and the position of planets appear to play an important role in Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav's decisions these days. Whether it is taking major political decisions or filing nomination papers, he is said to consider auspicious timings before moving ahead. On November 13, Akhilesh said in Lucknow that he would visit the Ram Temple in Ayodhya only after astrologers decide an auspicious time. He said the positions of the Sun, Moon and other stars would be checked before fixing the date. Political observers say Akhilesh has believed in astrology since his days as Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister. His wife, Dimple Yadav, also wears a five-faced Rudraksha necklace. According to a traditional belief, wearing a five-faced Rudraksha has a positive effect on one's husband. Astrology has been part of Akhilesh's political journey Akhilesh returned from Australia's University of Sydney in 1998 after completing a master's degree in engineering. In 2000, he entered active politics by winning the Lok Sabha by-election from Kannauj. In 2012, his father Mulayam Singh Yadav decided to project him as the Samajwadi Party's face for the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. Akhilesh planned to take out a Rath Yatra across the state. It is said that the dates of his major political programmes were decided after checking whether the planets were in a favourable position. The party went on to form the government in Uttar Pradesh. When Akhilesh became Chief Minister for the first time on March 15, 2012, the date and time of his oath-taking ceremony were reportedly fixed after consulting astrologers. Special care was taken to decide the direction of the stage at La Martiniere College ground in Lucknow and the exact time of the ceremony. Vastu changes before moving into the Chief Minister's residence After becoming Chief Minister, Akhilesh did not immediately move into the official residence at 5, Kalidas Marg. He continued to stay at his private residence on Vikramaditya Marg for several months. Vastu and astrological reasons were said to be behind the delay. Before moving into the Kalidas Marg bungalow, several changes were reportedly made according to Vastu principles. The direction of the main entrance and the arrangement of rooms were changed. He then entered the house after a havan and prayers at an auspicious time. How 'Tipu' became Akhilesh Akhilesh was called 'Tipu' during his childhood. When he went to Dholpur Military School for admission, he needed a formal name. According to reports, his family priest and astrologers suggested the name 'Akhilesh' after studying his horoscope and the stars linked to his Cancer zodiac sign. His connection with Lalu Prasad Yadav's astrologer A well-known astrologer, Shankar Charan Tripathi, is said to have been close to Akhilesh. He was also known to be close to RJD chief Lalu Prasad Yadav and was related to the Yadav family through marriage. Reports say Akhilesh's horoscope was studied before the 2012 Assembly elections and after he became Chief Minister. During political difficulties, advice on religious rituals and prayers for peace among the planets was also taken through family astrologers. Astrologers reportedly decided nomination timings in 2022 and 2024 During the 2022 Assembly elections, Akhilesh filed his nomination from the Karhal seat. Reports say a priest had decided the time at which he should submit the papers. During the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, he reached the Kannauj district collectorate to file his nomination. Sources said he waited before handing over the papers because he was waiting for the auspicious time suggested by his priest. Akhilesh is also getting the Kedareshwar Temple built in Saifai, Etawah. The temple is being constructed on 11 acres of land. Reports say advice from priests in South India and Kashi was taken at every stage, from laying the foundation to the construction work. Priests from South India perform rituals at the temple. Akhilesh is also said to be in touch with astrologers from Kashi and Prayagraj. Earlier questioned for not visiting temples, now questioned for visiting them Senior journalist Suresh Bahadur Singh says seeking an auspicious time before starting important work is a common Hindu tradition. He says the Samajwadi Party and its leaders have always had faith in Hinduism, priests and astrology. Now, they are expressing this faith openly to show people that they also follow Sanatan traditions. Singh says Akhilesh was earlier questioned for not visiting temples, but now he is being criticised for visiting them. Being a secular party does not mean its leader has to give up his own religious beliefs. He also points to the large Hanuman temple in Saifai as a sign of Akhilesh's religious faith. According to Singh, politics has increasingly come to revolve around the '80-20' formula, referring to the Hindu and Muslim population. In such a situation, no party wants to upset the majority community while trying to appeal to one section of voters. 'It is wrong to view his faith only through politics' Political analyst Rajendra Kumar says Akhilesh is not the only leader who believes in astrology and religious rituals. Even senior BJP leaders follow such practices. He says the country is currently going through a phase of Hindutva politics, in which every leader is trying to openly show their religious identity. Kumar says that whether Akhilesh visits Noida or stays away from it does not affect the city's development. He adds that the discussion around Akhilesh avoiding Noida is based on an old belief. If Akhilesh follows religious practices and offers prayers, there is nothing wrong with it. A temple belongs to everyone, he says. How was the Samajwadi Party's politics different under Mulayam Singh Yadav? The Samajwadi Party's politics was different during Mulayam Singh Yadav's time. Mulayam presented himself as a strong follower of socialist leader Ram Manohar Lohia and as a secular leader. He respected saints and visited the Kumbh Mela, but did not leave political decisions to astrology or auspicious timings. For him, political calculations were the most important factor. Akhilesh, however, has changed the party's image over the years. To counter the BJP's Hindutva politics, Akhilesh has changed his approach. He started visiting temples more often after 2017. The Samajwadi Party won 37 Lok Sabha seats in Uttar Pradesh in the 2024 elections. His confidence in this approach is said to have grown after the victory. He wants to counter the allegations of appeasement often made against the Samajwadi Party. This is one reason he now speaks openly about his Hindu faith. He has also said that he belongs to the family line of Lord Krishna and follows Sanatan traditions. During election campaigns, Akhilesh's convoy now often stops outside temples, both big and small. He has visited Vindhyachal Dham, Chitrakoot and Kashi Vishwanath Temple. Religious leaders and saints are now often invited to the Samajwadi Party office. Akhilesh honours them with shawls and seeks their blessings.

stories.title: 6 prominent BJP faces may contest UP elections:Could pose a challenge to SP Congress; first list expected in Jan 2027
stories.summary: Big BJP leaders are expected to contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. They include several senior ministers and MLCs. The BJP's central leadership has taken this major decision to help the party reach the majority mark in the Assembly. It has been decided that: BJP leaders who have been members of the Rajya Sabha or Legislative Council (MLC) twice or more will not be given another opportunity in the Upper House. All such leaders will now have to prove themselves by contesting Lok Sabha or Assembly elections. According to BJP sources, the party's first list of candidates could be released in January 2027. It may include the names of Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya, Jal Shakti Minister Swatantra Dev Singh, MSME Minister Bhupendra Singh Chaudhary and Energy Minister Arvind Kumar Sharma. The BJP leadership believes that fielding prominent faces from the government and the organisation in elections will make it easier to put the Samajwadi Party (SP) and Congress on the defensive. Here are five reasons behind the strategy: 1. Keeping the Opposition occupied in certain constituencies: When prominent leaders such as a Deputy Chief Minister, senior minister or former state president contest from a constituency, opposition parties cannot afford to give them an easy walkover. To take on such a heavyweight, the Opposition has to deploy a large number of its top star campaigners, strategists and election resources. As a result, its senior leaders and resources remain occupied in a few select 'high-profile' constituencies, reducing the pressure on ordinary seats. 2. Benefits in neighbouring constituencies: A prominent leader's influence is not limited to their own constituency. For example, if AK Sharma contests from the Madhuban seat in Mau or Bhupendra Chaudhary contests from a constituency in western UP, their rallies, roadshows and media coverage could directly influence eight to 10 Assembly constituencies in the region and nearby areas. Ordinary candidates from those constituencies could also benefit. 3. Easier to manage caste equations: Prominent leaders have their own caste and social identities. When an influential leader is given a ticket from a particular region, it sends a message to voters from that community across the state that the party values their leadership. This can help keep voters united. 4. Countering anti-incumbency: In several constituencies, people are unhappy with their local MLAs, and the Opposition tries to take advantage of this. In such a situation, replacing the sitting MLA with a senior minister or prominent leader can help reduce local resentment to a considerable extent. 5. Keeping factionalism among workers in check: Factionalism within the organisation often becomes a reason for electoral defeats. When a heavyweight leader contests as a candidate, booth-level workers become active and put in their full effort. The stature of a senior leader can overshadow local factionalism, making it difficult for the Opposition to compete at the booth level. Find out which constituencies these leaders are preparing to contest from According to party sources, Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya may contest from the Prayagraj North Assembly constituency. He has stepped up direct interactions with workers in the area. He sent them Diwali greetings and has been strengthening his connections by attending events related to their personal joys, difficulties and bereavements. Harshvardhan Bajpai of the BJP is the sitting MLA from this constituency. Energy and Urban Development Minister Arvind Kumar Sharma has been a member of the Legislative Council for two consecutive terms. His current term ends on 30 January 2027. Whether he will contest the Assembly elections or return to the Upper House is a decision that the Prime Minister's Office will take. His increasing activity in the Madhuban Assembly constituency in recent months has fuelled speculation that he may contest from there. He belongs to the Bhumihar community. The party believes that fielding him from Madhuban could help consolidate Bhumihar votes not only in Mau but also in the Ghazipur and Varanasi regions. Ramvilas Chauhan of the BJP is currently the MLA from Madhuban. BJP MSME Minister Bhupendra Singh Chaudhary is a resident of Moradabad, but the social and caste equations there are not considered favourable to him. According to party sources, he may contest from the Garhmukteshwar Assembly constituency in Hapur district. The constituency has the highest number of Muslim and Dalit voters. However, candidates backed by upper-caste and Jat voters find it easier to win. Polarisation among Hindu voters makes the seat more secure. Harendra Singh Teotia of the BJP is the sitting MLA from Garhmukteshwar. According to political observers, the Madihan and Chunar constituencies in his home district of Mirzapur are considered safe options for Jal Shakti Minister Swatantra Dev Singh. Both seats have a sizeable Kurmi population and are currently held by the BJP. In contrast, his supporters are discussing the possibility of him contesting from the Madhaugarh or Kalpi seats in Jalaun, where he has built his political career. However, the caste equations there do not appear to be favourable to him. The Kushwaha community has the strongest presence in Madhaugarh, which also has around 1.25 lakh Dalit, 50,000 Brahmin, 32,000 Thakur and 14,000 Yadav voters. In Kalpi, rebel SP leader Vinod Chaturvedi is the MLA. The constituency has around 70,000 Dalit, 60,000 Pal-Baghel, 50,000 Thakur, 45,000 Brahmin and 35,000 Muslim voters. Dr Mahendra Singh, considered one of the BJP's key election strategists, may also be fielded in the Assembly elections this time. He has been a member of the Legislative Council for three consecutive terms. According to sources, Mahendra Singh is exploring the possibility of contesting from Lucknow or a constituency in his home district of Pratapgarh. Dinesh Pratap Singh, Minister of State (Independent Charge), who joined the BJP after leaving the Congress, has lost Lok Sabha elections twice from the Rae Bareli constituency. The party is now preparing to field him in the Assembly elections. He may be given a ticket from the Harchandpur Assembly constituency in Rae Bareli district. In the 2022 Assembly elections, his brother Rakesh Pratap Singh contested from this seat but lost to the SP's Rahul Lodhi. Former MPs and Union ministers are also staking claims for tickets It is not just senior ministers in the state government. Union ministers, former MPs and several key office-bearers of the organisation are also staking claims to contest the UP Assembly elections. stories.title: Owaisi says 'will no longer bow before any party':Supporters chant 'Sher aaya, sher aaya' and throw fake notes at Meerut rally
stories.summary: AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi reached Meerut and addressed a public meeting at Nauchandi Ground. Supporters welcomed him with slogans of "Look, look, who has arrived… The lion has arrived, the lion has arrived." A large number of supporters gathered at the venue. This was Owaisi's first major public meeting in Meerut after his party formed an alliance with the Azad Samaj Party. During his address, Owaisi appealed to people to unite against injustice. He said that if people did not want innocent young men to lose their lives because of false cases, they would have to come together. "We are extending our hand. You should join hands with us. We will end this injustice. How long will people continue to suffer like this?" he said. Owaisi asked people to help AIMIM and Azad Samaj Party candidates win from Meerut in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections and send them to the Assembly. He said political awareness had now increased and that they would no longer bow before any political party or beg for support. He added that both parties would work together and use their unity and strength to succeed. Owaisi also welcomed Bhim Army national president Vinay Ratan Singh on the stage. He said Chandrashekhar Azad could not attend the meeting due to his busy schedule. The meeting is being seen as an important event for the alliance ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. The crowd and the involvement of party workers are expected to give an idea of the alliance's support in the region. Owaisi responded to a BJP leader's remark mocking the alliance of a “man with a moustache and a man with a beard”. He said, “I am saying that this will harm the clean-shaven face. If you provoke us, we will not spare you.” Referring to the 2014, 2017, 2019, 2022 and 2024 elections, Owaisi said he and Chandrashekhar Azad would now come together to challenge the BJP. He also took a dig at Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav over his PDA slogan, saying, “The real meaning of PDA is ‘Palat Diya Akhilesh’ (Akhilesh has been overthrown).” Owaisi further alleged that 50,000 people were displaced during the 2013 Muzaffarnagar riots when Akhilesh Yadav was the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh. He claimed that despite having 47 Muslim MLAs, the Samajwadi Party did not help the victims or even speak up for them. Owaisi also accused Akhilesh of watching performances by artists invited from Mumbai at Saifai while people affected by the riots were struggling. This report is being updated…

stories.title: India wins Asia Cup under Gonda's Lakshya's captaincy:Beats Pakistan in U-19 final; father says victory will be remembered for years
stories.summary: India's Under-19 team won the Asia Cup under the captaincy of Gonda's Lakshya Raichandani. The team defeated Pakistan by one wicket in the final played in Al Amerat, UAE, on Saturday. As soon as India secured the win, celebrations broke out at Lakshya's home and across Gonda district. His family and local residents burst firecrackers to celebrate the victory. People also welcomed his father with garlands. Lakshya, 17, received praise from his family and people in the district for leading the team to victory. His father said, "My son's victory will be remembered for years. All the players put in an excellent performance." Won the final while chasing a target of 338 runs Rajesh Raichandani, a resident of Guddoomāl Chauraha, and his wife, Lakshmi Raichandani, are BJP leaders. Their 17-year-old son, Lakshya, is the captain of India's Under-19 team. The Asia Cup final was played in Al Amerat, UAE, under Lakshya's captaincy. Pakistan set India a target of 338 runs. India won the match by one wicket after hitting a four off the final ball. Lakshya was given the responsibility of leading the Indian Under-19 team in the tournament. Under his captaincy, the team defeated Pakistan to lift the Asia Cup title. Father says, "This is the victory of the entire team" Lakshya's father, Rajesh Raichandani, said the entire family was delighted with India's victory under his son's leadership. He said Pakistan had set India a target of 338 runs. Mohit hit a four off the final ball to secure a one-wicket win for India. He added that India's victory over Pakistan would be remembered for years. He said the victory was not just his son's achievement but a win for the entire Indian team. stories.title: Divya Mittal visits Narathua, listens to women's concerns:Locals welcome Jan Niti Bharat Party national president
stories.summary: Jan Niti Bharat Party national president and former IAS officer Divya Mittal visited the Shiva temple in Narathua village of Aurai block. She offered prayers at the temple, where locals welcomed her with flower garlands and traditional scarves around noon. Those who welcomed her included Manish Tiwari, Nitish Choubey, Sarvesh Shukla, the village head of Matkipur, Mukesh Dubey, Rakesh Bind and the former village head of Narathua. Several women from the village were also present. Divya Mittal met the locals and listened to the problems faced by women. During her address, Mittal said she had earlier served as the District Magistrate of Mirzapur. She said she had worked abroad before deciding to serve in India after completing her studies. After becoming an IAS officer, she worked in several districts. She said that while serving as a District Magistrate, she would first meet women during her village visits and listen to their problems. She would then work with department officials to find solutions. Mittal said she had started this initiative to understand the problems of poor and needy people and work for public welfare. She appealed to people to raise their voices for each other's problems without discrimination and work together. She said the country would move forward if people came together. Nitish Choubey, Sarvesh Shukla, Manish Tiwari, former Aurai Bar Association president Mukesh Dubey, Anurag Dubey, the former village head and several women attended the programme.

stories.title: Yogi says Meerut was once known for 'mafiaraj' 'katta':Doubles gallantry awards; raises stamp duty exemption for soldiers to ₹50 lakh
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath attended a reunion event for ex-servicemen in Meerut on Saturday. During the event, he announced that the cash rewards and yearly payments given to soldiers receiving gallantry awards will be doubled. He also announced that the stamp duty exemption on house purchases by soldiers will be increased from ₹20 lakh to ₹50 lakh. In addition, eligible family members of soldiers who die in service will now get government jobs in their home district or a nearby district. Yogi said that soldiers never retire from their duty towards the country. "Their uniform changes, but their resolve does not," he said. 5 major announcements by CM Yogi The one-time cash reward and yearly payment given to soldiers receiving gallantry awards will be doubled. The stamp duty exemption on house purchases by soldiers will be increased from ₹20 lakh to ₹50 lakh. Eligible family members of soldiers who die in service will get government jobs in their home district or a nearby district. Yogi said Meerut was earlier known for mafia rule, illegal weapons, vehicle theft and illegal tree cutting. Today, the city is making a name for itself in the sports goods industry. He said there was no place for terrorists and anti-national forces in the country. He added that the government was responsible for the safety and welfare of soldiers. 'There is no place for anti-national forces in the country' Yogi said there was no place for terrorists and anti-national forces in the country. He said they had already been buried in the soil. Addressing ex-servicemen, he said they had given the best years of their lives to protect the country. Now, the responsibility for their safety and welfare lies with the double-engine government, which will fulfil this duty. 'Family members will get jobs in their home district' The Chief Minister announced a change in the rules for giving government jobs to family members of soldiers who die in service. Now, an eligible family member will be given a job in the soldier's home district or a nearby district. Stamp duty exemption to increase to ₹50 lakh Yogi also announced an increase in the stamp duty exemption for soldiers buying houses. At present, the exemption is available on houses valued up to ₹20 lakh. This limit will now be increased to ₹50 lakh.

stories.title: Leave for women civic staff on Chhath:Lucknow Mayor announces special Holiday on November 16
stories.summary: All women employees of the Lucknow Municipal Corporation and Jal Kal Department will get a special one-day leave on Monday, November 16, on the occasion of Chhath Mahaparv. Mayor Sushma Kharkwal took this decision keeping in mind the religious beliefs of the women employees and the importance of the festival. Women observe a 36-hour waterless fast The mayor issued a letter to the municipal commissioner on Saturday, asking him to make arrangements for the special leave. In the letter, she said Chhath Mahaparv is an important festival of faith and tradition, which women celebrate with great devotion. During the festival, women observe a 36-hour fast without drinking water. They also make preparations for the rituals and prasad. Festival to end with prayers to the rising sun The festival will conclude on Monday, November 16, with prayers and offerings to the rising sun. The mayor has directed officials to grant special leave to all women employees so they can celebrate the festival with their families.

stories.title: Bride dies 12 hours after wedding farewell in UP:Married Instagram friend; brother alleges husband killed her
stories.summary: A 23-year-old bride was found dead in Mau, Uttar Pradesh, just 12 hours after leaving her parental home following the wedding farewell. Her brother has accused her 28-year-old husband of strangling her over dowry. He alleged that the groom wanted a motorcycle and another ₹50,000. The bride, Aska, had married Harishchandra, a man she met on Instagram, seven months ago. It was a love marriage. Since then, she had been living at her parental home in Azamgarh. On Friday at around 10 pm, Harishchandra took Aska to his home for the first time after the wedding farewell. On Saturday at around 10 am, a neighbour of Harishchandra and Aska's cousin (her paternal aunt's daughter) called her family and informed them about the incident. The bride's family then reached the house and informed the police. Police have detained Harishchandra and are questioning him. The incident took place in the Ghosi Kotwali area, around 25 km from the Mau district headquarters. She made Instagram reels, where she met Harishchandra Aska was from Sikraula village in Azamgarh. She was the youngest of three brothers and two sisters. Two of her brothers are not married yet. Harishchandra Chauhan has four brothers and one sister. Two of the brothers in his family are married. Aska made videos on Instagram. A year ago, she became friends on Instagram with Harishchandra, who was from Dera Ghat village in Mau. The two gradually began an affair. The two decided to get married. Their families also agreed. They got married on 7 May. After the wedding, Aska continued to live at her parents' home. On the night of 13 November, Harishchandra brought her to his home after the farewell ceremony. The paternal aunt's daughter called and said, "The bride has died" Aska's paternal aunt's daughter was married in Harishchandra's village. This morning, she called Aska's family and said, "Aska has died." The family then hurried to the spot, where they found her body lying in a room. Brother said, "Blood was coming from my sister's mouth and nose" Aska's brother Guddu Chauhan said, "Blood was coming from my sister's mouth and nose. My brother-in-law and his family beat my sister. Her in-laws were harassing her. We had given everything at the wedding, including a double bed, cooler, refrigerator, washing machine and flour mill, but they demanded his motorcycle and another ₹50,000. My brother-in-law had argued with me several times over the phone even before her departure. She was assaulted after she left." Station in-charge says the cause of death will be known from the post-mortem report Kotwal Ravindranath Rai said it is not yet clear under what circumstances the death occurred. Police are investigating all aspects. The forensic team has collected evidence from the scene. The cause of death will become clear only after the post-mortem report is received. ---------------------------------- Tell us in the survey whether your MLA works or not... stories.title: Yogi leads 'Jai Shri Ram' chants at minister's engagement:Sandeep Singh and his brother exchange rings with their fiancées in Aligarh
stories.summary: The first picture of Uttar Pradesh Education Minister Sandeep Singh with his bride-to-be, Meghna Chaudhary, has surfaced. The couple will get engaged in Aligarh today (November 14). Meghna's family reached Aligarh on Friday evening. Guests from both families are staying at the Lemon Tree Hotel on Marris Road. Sandeep Singh welcomed Meghna along with his family. In the picture, Sandeep Singh is seen wearing a black kurta, while Meghna is wearing a dark brown suit and holding a rose garland. Sandeep Singh's younger brother, Saurabh Singh, will also get engaged during the ceremony. Several prominent leaders, including Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, are expected to attend the event. The minister has invited 80,000 guests to the ceremony. Arrangements made for meals for 80,000 guests At the engagement ceremony in Aligarh, 60 types of dishes, including pumpkin puri, are being prepared for the guests. The guests have also started arriving. The family of Saurabh Singh's bride, Antara Tyagi, had also arrived in Aligarh on Thursday night. Arrangements have been made to provide meals for around 80,000 guests and parking for 657 cars at the event. Now, here are the arrangements being made... Separate arrangements for VIPs and ordinary guests The pandal has been divided into separate sections according to the categories of guests. Four stages have been set up across the venue. Two of them are for cultural programmes. One main stage has been prepared for the two brothers and their future life partners. The fourth stage has been set up for VIP guests. Arrangements have been made for seating and hospitality for distinguished guests in the VIP section. A separate area has been created for ordinary guests. It will have arrangements for seating, meals and viewing the programmes. A canopy and buffet gallery have also been prepared. Event venue 881 feet wide and 1,033 feet long Preparations for the event have been made at the approximately 100-bigha field located on Ramghat Kalyan Marg. According to the available layout, the premises are approximately 881 feet wide and 1,033 feet long. Separate sections have been created for guests' seating, food, accommodation and event management. The VIP cottage covers an area of approximately 123×50 feet, the kitchen measures 80×60 feet and a tent for drivers has been set up over an area of approximately 100×80 feet. Separate tents, a green room, a medical room, a control area and toilets have been arranged for staff accommodation. Barricades and entry and exit routes have also been set up in different parts of the premises. Parking has been arranged for 657 cars. In addition, a 100×80-foot drivers' tent, labour tent, flower tent, green room, washrooms and medical room have been prepared. A control area and barricading have been arranged around the stage. 500 employees engaged in decoration work The decoration and tent arrangements for the ceremony have been entrusted to a company from Moradabad. The company has subcontracted the work to a firm in Noida. Artisans have been brought in from Delhi, Mumbai and Rajasthan for the decorations. Around 500 employees have been deployed for the preparations. Large air conditioners, generators, round tables and equipment for the guests' convenience have been installed at the venue. 60 dishes on the menu, including Kalyan Singh's favourite vegetable dish Vivek Premi's team from Premi Caterers is responsible for the guests' food. Around 60 dishes have been included on the menu. These include 11 sweets and 11 varieties of vegetables. Former Chief Minister Kalyan Singh's favourite pumpkin and potato vegetable dish will also be prepared. Seven kitchens have been set up for the regular meals. A separate kitchen will be maintained for VIP guests, where chefs brought in from Delhi will prepare the food. Around 1,000 chefs, assistants and waiters have been deployed for the catering arrangements. Food has been arranged for approximately 80,000 guests at the event. Several leaders from Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand may attend Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Governor Anandiben Patel and both Deputy Chief Ministers, Brajesh Pathak and Keshav Prasad Maurya, are expected to attend the ceremony. Besides them, Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami, Dinesh Sharma and Santosh Gangwar, along with several political leaders and VIPs, have been invited. Kailash Kher to perform Popular singer Kailash Kher will arrive at the engagement ceremony with his team. He will give a special performance on stage at the ceremony. His programme has been finalised. Special arrangements are being made on stage for it. 3 helipads built at different locations, Dhanipur airstrip the main hub The Dhanipur airstrip has been designated as the main hub for guests arriving by air. A helipad has been prepared at the PAC ground on Ramghat Road. Another helipad has also been built on the Global Residency Bypass. Prateek Bhushan Singh, son of former MP Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, is likely to arrive here. These locations may also be used for other distinguished guests as required. 3 ASPs, 7 COs and 700 police personnel to handle security In view of the VVIP movement and the arrival of a large number of guests, the security arrangements have been divided into eight zones. Police personnel will be deployed under the leadership of SSP Neeraj Jadaun. Three additional SPs, seven COs and around 700 inspectors, sub-inspectors and police personnel have been requisitioned from neighbouring districts. The additional force will handle security alongside the local police. Entry to the VIP lounge and the areas designated for distinguished guests will be controlled. Barricades have been arranged at around 38 locations. Cranes are also being prepared for deployment to manage VVIP movement and traffic. Schools on Ramghat Kalyan Marg to remain closed In view of the event and VIP movement, around half a dozen schools within a 150-metre radius of the venue have declared a holiday today. Other schools operating on Ramghat Kalyan Marg will also remain closed. Rakesh Nandan, the director of Heritage International School, has confirmed that the school will remain closed. Wedding in Delhi on 26 November, reception on 27 November The weddings of both brothers will be held on 26 November at The Leela Hotel in Delhi. The reception will be held on 27 November at the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium, also in Delhi. The Prime Minister, along with several prominent leaders and distinguished guests from across the country, is expected to attend these events.

stories.title: Lawyers' protest causes traffic jam in Lucknow:Hundreds of vehicles stuck as barricades block major roads
stories.summary: Lawyers will take to the streets in Lucknow on Saturday, demanding the implementation of the Advocates Protection Act. They have announced a march on foot and a siege of the Legislative Assembly over the demand. Several lawyers' organisations across the state have extended their support to the Assembly siege programme. A large number of lawyers are expected to participate. The march will begin at the court complex in Kaisarbagh. From there, the lawyers will reach Parivartan Chowk. They will then proceed towards the Legislative Assembly via Atal Chowk. The lawyers' main objective is to convey their demand to the government and put pressure on it to implement the Advocates Protection Act. Meanwhile, the police administration is also on alert in view of the lawyers' protest and announcement of the Assembly siege. A large number of police personnel have been deployed along the march route and in surrounding areas. Additional security forces, along with police from several police stations, have also been deployed to manage security arrangements.

stories.title: School bus brakes fail in Rishikesh, crashes into wall:27 children from UP escape unhurt, principal among 3 injured
stories.summary: A school bus carrying 27 children from Uttar Pradesh crashed into a roadside wall after its brakes failed at the PWD intersection in Muni Ki Reti, Rishikesh, on Saturday morning. The driver, helper and school principal sustained minor injuries, while all 27 children escaped unharmed. According to police, the bus (UP 83 AT 8300) was carrying students and teachers from Pandit Tilak Bhanu Senior Secondary School in Firozabad to Lakshman Jhula. The children were travelling to the area for a bath and sightseeing. At around 9:40 am, the bus's brakes suddenly failed at the PWD intersection. The driver lost control of the vehicle, which crashed into a roadside wall. Driver, helper and principal taken to hospital After receiving information about the accident, Muni Ki Reti police reached the spot and evacuated everyone from the bus. The driver, Jaiprakash, helper Awadhesh and school principal Rajni Saraswat were taken to hospital, where they received first aid. Police arranged accommodation for the children at Madhuban Ashram and also made arrangements for their food and drinking water. Police personnel helped teachers look after the children. Bus had earlier been fined for overloading According to police, the bus was carrying more passengers than its permitted capacity. Earlier, ARTO Rashmi Pant had taken action against the vehicle and asked 21 additional passengers to get off. The bus was also fined for overloading. Accidents reported earlier at the downhill intersection The steep gradient at the PWD intersection is also being considered a possible reason for accidents at the spot. Several accidents have reportedly occurred there in the past. Police said they had already written to the concerned department, asking it to take steps to repair the road and address the problem. Police are currently investigating the accident and taking necessary legal action.

stories.title: Premanand Maharaj resumes foot march after 7 months:Devotees shower flowers along 1-km route, welcome him with fireworks
stories.summary: A large crowd of devotees gathered during religious leader Premanand Maharaj's foot march in Vrindavan on Saturday morning. Devotees lined up along nearly 1 km of the Parikrama Marg to catch a glimpse of him. They welcomed him by laying flowers along the route and bursting fireworks at several places. Chants of 'Radhe Radhe' and 'Shri Harivansh' echoed throughout. Premanand had travelled from the Yamuna Bihar Kunj Ashram in Belvan, across the Yamuna, to the Keli Kunj Ashram in Vrindavan. After seeing the crowd along the Parikrama Marg, he stepped out of his vehicle and began walking towards the ashram. A similar scene was witnessed during his foot march for the first time in nearly seven months. Crossed the Yamuna by steamer to reach Vrindavan Premanand Maharaj left the Yamuna Bihar Kunj Ashram in Belvan with his entourage on Saturday morning. He first travelled by car to the banks of the Yamuna. From there, he crossed the river by steamer and reached the Parikrama Marg in Vrindavan. A large number of devotees were already waiting for him. Seeing the crowd, Maharaj stepped out of his vehicle and began walking towards the Keli Kunj Ashram. See three pictures... Ropes used to control the crowd As Premanand began walking, devotees moved forward to catch a glimpse of him. To manage the crowd, ashram volunteers tied ropes along both sides of the road to create a passage. Despite these arrangements, devotees remained eager to see him. Police personnel and ashram volunteers had to make considerable efforts to escort him safely to the ashram. The crowd continued to grow as the foot march progressed. Foot march scene seen again after May Saturday's gathering and the welcome arrangements reminded devotees of a similar scene from nearly seven months ago. Until May, devotees used to welcome him in the same way during his foot marches by laying flowers along the route. Had travelled on a Bullet for meditation on Bhai Dooj On Bhai Dooj, Premanand travelled on a Bullet motorcycle to the banks of the Yamuna for meditation. His disciple and former wrestler Rinku Singh was riding the motorcycle. The secluded spot where Maharaj went for meditation was inaccessible by car. After completing his meditation, he returned to the Yamuna Bihar Kunj Ashram. Devotees got to see him after 34 days. Premanand Maharaj has been living in seclusion for months Premanand has been living in seclusion for the past few months. He is currently staying at the Yamuna Bihar Kunj Ashram near Belvan, across the Yamuna. The ashram is spread over approximately 9.5 bighas. Most of its area is covered with greenery, while construction occupies around 25% of the premises. Maharaj also undergoes dialysis at the ashram.

stories.title: Bus catches fire on Yamuna Expressway in Mathura:40 passengers evacuated safely; bus and luggage gutted in fire
stories.summary: A moving bus caught fire on the Yamuna Expressway in Mathura at around 1:30 am on Saturday. Passengers raised an alarm after noticing flames. All 40 passengers were evacuated safely before the fire could spread further. Police and fire brigade teams rushed to the spot after receiving information. The fire was brought under control after nearly one-and-a-half hours of effort. The bus and passengers' belongings were destroyed in the blaze. No injuries or casualties were reported. The incident took place in the Raya police station area. See 2 pictures... Bus was travelling from Delhi to Chhatarpur According to information, the bus (MP14ZH5063) belonged to Khajuraho Travels. Driver Jitendra, son of Mohanlal and a resident of Nowgong in Chhatarpur district, Madhya Pradesh, was travelling with around 40 passengers from Kashmere Gate in Delhi to Chhatarpur. While crossing the Raya Cut bridge in the Raya police station area, a short circuit in the bus's wiring triggered the fire. The flames spread rapidly, engulfing the bus and passengers' belongings. Passengers panicked after seeing the fire and rushed out to save their lives. Police received information at 1:38 am According to police, PRV 5840 received information about the fire at around 1:38 am on Saturday. The station house officer reached the spot with police personnel and alerted the fire brigade. Fire engines arrived shortly afterwards and began firefighting operations. After nearly one-and-a-half hours, firefighters brought the blaze completely under control. All passengers were evacuated safely. CO says all passengers evacuated safely Mahavan Circle Officer Sanjeev Kumar Rai said no formal complaint had been received in the matter. Further legal action will be taken if a complaint is filed.

stories.title: 5 more special trains to run via Gorakhpur for Chhath:Services announced from Chhapra to Mumbai and Delhi and Sitamarhi to Anand Vihar
stories.summary: Railways has decided to operate five additional special trains to help passengers travelling home for Chhath Puja and returning to their workplaces after the festival. Of these, three trains will run from Chhapra to Lokmanya Tilak Terminus, Delhi and New Delhi. The other two will operate between Ludhiana and Katihar, and Sitamarhi and Anand Vihar Terminal. All five trains will pass through Gorakhpur. This will provide relief to passengers from Gorakhpur, Basti, Gonda, Deoria and nearby districts travelling towards Delhi, Mumbai, Punjab and Bihar. According to the schedule released by the Railways, the 05083/05084 Chhapra-Lokmanya Tilak Terminus-Chhapra Special will make two trips. The Chhapra-Delhi and Chhapra-New Delhi special trains will each make one trip. Meanwhile, the 04670 Ludhiana-Katihar Special will operate one-way on November 14. The 05519 Sitamarhi-Anand Vihar Terminal Special will also make one trip on November 17. Special train to Mumbai from Chhapra on two days The 05083 Chhapra-Lokmanya Tilak Terminus Special will depart from Chhapra at 8 pm on November 16 and 21. It will pass through Mashrakh, Dighwa Dubauli, Gopalganj, Thawe, Tamkuhi Road, Padrauna, Ramkola, Kaptanganj and Pipraich before reaching Gorakhpur at 2:35 am the following day. From Gorakhpur, it will pass through Basti, Gonda, Gomti Nagar, Aishbagh, Kanpur Central, Virangana Lakshmibai Jhansi, Bina, Rani Kamlapati, Itarsi, Khandwa, Bhusaval, Nashik Road, Igatpuri and Kalyan before reaching Lokmanya Tilak Terminus at noon on the third day. On its return journey, the 05084 Lokmanya Tilak Terminus-Chhapra Special will depart at 3 pm on November 18 and 23. It will reach Chhapra at 5:45 am on the third day and Gorakhpur at 10:55 pm on the second day. The train will have 22 coaches, including 16 sleeper, two third AC economy, one third AC and one second AC coach. It will also have two generator-cum-luggage coaches. Chhapra-Delhi Special to run on November 17 The 05071 Chhapra-Delhi Special will depart from Chhapra at 8:05 pm on November 17. It will pass through Mashrakh, Dighwa Dubauli, Gopalganj, Thawe, Tamkuhi Road, Padrauna, Ramkola, Kaptanganj and Pipraich before reaching Gorakhpur at 2:20 am the following day. From there, it will pass through Khalilabad, Basti, Gonda, Burhwal, Sitapur, Shahjahanpur, Bareilly, Moradabad and Ghaziabad before reaching Delhi at 5:15 pm. On its return journey, the 05072 Delhi-Chhapra Special will depart from Delhi at 8:10 pm on November 18. It will reach Gorakhpur at 10:30 am the following day and Chhapra at 5 pm. The train will have 22 coaches, including five sleeper, four general, two third AC economy, six third AC, two second AC and one first-cum-second AC coach. It will also have a generator-cum-luggage coach and a Divyangjan-friendly coach. Chhapra-New Delhi Special to run on November 18 and 19 The 05073 Chhapra-New Delhi Special will depart from Chhapra at 11:05 pm on November 18. It will pass through Mashrakh, Dighwa Dubauli, Gopalganj, Thawe, Tamkuhi Road, Padrauna, Ramkola, Kaptanganj and Pipraich before reaching Gorakhpur at 5:20 am on November 19. It will then pass through Khalilabad, Basti, Gonda, Burhwal, Sitapur, Shahjahanpur, Bareilly, Moradabad and Ghaziabad before reaching New Delhi at 8:15 pm. On its return journey, the 05074 New Delhi-Chhapra Special will depart from New Delhi at 11:10 pm on November 19. It will reach Gorakhpur at 1:30 pm the following day and Chhapra at 8 pm. The train will have 20 coaches, including eight third AC economy, eight sleeper and two general coaches. It will also have a generator-cum-luggage coach and a Divyangjan-friendly coach. Ludhiana-Katihar Special to run on November 14 The 04670 Ludhiana-Katihar Special will depart from Ludhiana at 6:30 am on November 14. It will pass through Dhandari Kalan, Sirhind, Rajpura, Ambala Cantt, Yamunanagar Jagadhri, Saharanpur, Moradabad, Bareilly, Shahjahanpur, Sitapur, Burhwal and Gonda before reaching Basti at 11:12 pm. From there, it will pass through Khalilabad and reach Gorakhpur at 1 am on November 15. The train will then travel through Deoria Sadar, Bhatni, Siwan and Chhapra, followed by Sonpur, Hajipur, Bachhwara, Barauni, Khagaria and Mansi, before reaching Katihar at 2 pm. The train will have 21 coaches, including eight sleeper, 11 general and two Divyangjan-friendly coaches. Sitamarhi-Anand Vihar Special to run on November 17 The 05519 Sitamarhi-Anand Vihar Terminal Special will depart from Sitamarhi at 11:50 am on November 17. It will pass through Bairgania, Ghorasahan, Raxaul, Sikta, Narkatiaganj, Bagaha and Siswa Bazar before reaching Kaptanganj at 6:17 pm. It will reach Gorakhpur at 7:25 pm. From there, it will pass through Gonda, Lucknow (Northern Railway), Moradabad and Ghaziabad before reaching Anand Vihar Terminal at 9:15 am the following day. The train will have 21 coaches, including 10 third AC, five sleeper and four general coaches. It will also have one SLRD coach and one generator-cum-luggage coach.

stories.title: Rain alert in UP today and tomorrow:Night temperature to drop by 2°C; Kanpur, Hardoi among 20 coldest cities
stories.summary: The effects of snowfall in Jammu and Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh are also being felt in Uttar Pradesh. Over the past 24 hours, the minimum temperature remained below 15 degrees in 20 cities, including Kanpur and Hardoi. According to IMD Lucknow, the minimum temperature will fall by another 2 degrees over the next five days. According to the Meteorological Department, some districts in western Uttar Pradesh may receive rain today and tomorrow, 15 November, due to a western disturbance. Meanwhile, fog blanketed 25 cities, including Lucknow, on Saturday morning. Weather pictures- Fog in the morning, light haze during the day According to Lucknow meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh, fog may persist in the mornings for the next five days. Light haze is likely to be seen during the day. The weather is expected to remain mainly dry in the coming days. Weather may be favourable for wheat sowing The drop in temperature will also affect farming activities. This period is particularly important for farmers preparing to cultivate wheat. Wheat is a major rabi crop, and timely sowing is considered crucial for a good yield. Pollution causes problems in Noida and Ghaziabad While temperatures are expected to fall across the state, air pollution remains a problem in Noida and Ghaziabad. Ghaziabad District Magistrate Ravindra Kumar has banned construction and demolition work until 20 November to control pollution. Meanwhile, in Noida and Greater Noida, schools up to Class V have been directed to operate in hybrid mode due to pollution. Under this arrangement, children will have the option of attending school for in-person classes or taking classes online. What is the Air Quality Index (AQI)? It is a score that indicates the quality of the air and helps us understand whether the air around us is clean or polluted. The AQI measures the levels of pollutants present in the air. The higher the AQI, the more hazardous the air is considered to be, and the greater the health risk. Understand it through the graphic below- How does poor AQI affect our health? When the AQI is poor, pollutants such as PM2.5, PM10, nitrogen dioxide, sulphur dioxide and ozone in the air penetrate deep into our lungs. These particles spread throughout the body through the bloodstream. They can cause various health problems, ranging from immediate to long-term effects. Continuous exposure reduces lung capacity and increases the risk of chronic diseases. Understand this through the graphic below:

stories.title: UP transfers 38 IAS officers, replaces 5 DMs:Joginder Singh appointed Bijnor DM; Prathamesh Kumar gets charge of Sitapur
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government transferred 38 IAS officers late on Friday, including five district magistrates (DMs), in a major administrative reshuffle. Bijnor DM Umesh Pratap Singh, Muzaffarnagar DM Umesh Mishra and Sitapur DM Raja Ganapati R have been removed from their district postings and given new assignments in the state government. According to sources, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath was not satisfied with their performance. Prathamesh Kumar has been appointed Sitapur DM, Sunil Singh Muzaffarnagar DM and Joginder Singh Bijnor DM. The government has also transferred the DMs of Siddharthnagar and Maharajganj. Gaurav Singh Sogarwal, who was serving as Siddharthnagar DM, has been appointed Maharajganj DM. Shivsharanappa GN, previously Maharajganj DM, will take charge in Siddharthnagar. The transfers are reportedly part of preparations for the Assembly elections. Officers who have held the same post for more than three years have been moved. See the list... CM's special secretary Anuj Singh appointed LDA vice-chairman Anuj Singh, who was serving as special secretary to the Chief Minister, has been appointed vice-chairman of the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA). He will now oversee urban development, infrastructure projects and action against illegal constructions in the state capital. Municipal commissioners of Varanasi and Ghaziabad changed Varanasi Municipal Commissioner Himanshu Nagpal has been transferred to Ghaziabad in the same capacity. Shashwat Tripurari, who was serving as Chief Development Officer (CDO) of Gorakhpur, has been appointed the new municipal commissioner of Varanasi. Ghaziabad Municipal Commissioner Vikramaditya Singh Malik has been appointed vice-chairman of the Meerut Development Authority. Three former DMs given new assignments in the government The three district magistrates removed from their posts have received new responsibilities: Prathamesh Kumar moves from LDA to Sitapur as DM Prathamesh Kumar, who was serving as vice-chairman of the Lucknow Development Authority, has been promoted and appointed District Magistrate of Sitapur. 2019 and 2020-batch officers receive new responsibilities Most of the 38 IAS officers transferred belong to the 2019 and 2020 batches. They have been assigned new roles as Additional Municipal Commissioners, Chief Development Officers (CDOs) in districts, Additional Commissioners in divisions and Additional Chief Executive Officers (ACEOs) in development authorities. Major reshuffle in Noida, Greater Noida and Yamuna authorities The government has also changed ACEOs in three major National Capital Region (NCR) development authorities — Noida, Greater Noida and the Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority (YEIDA). Yamuna Authority (YEIDA): Sanjay Kumar Meena, previously vice-chairman of the Meerut Development Authority, Krishna Kumar Singh, former CDO of Ayodhya, and Shatrohan Vaishya, former CDO of Firozabad, have been appointed ACEOs. Greater Noida Authority: Nupur Goyal, previously CDO of Meerut, and Praveen Verma, former ACEO of the Bundelkhand Development Authority, have been appointed ACEOs. Soumya Srivastava has been relieved of the additional charge of Officer on Special Duty (OSD) at the Greater Noida Authority. Noida Authority: Vandana Tripathi has been transferred from the post of ACEO to become Additional Commissioner of the Saharanpur division. Preeti Jaiswal, who was serving as Additional Commissioner in Bareilly, has been appointed the new ACEO of the Noida Authority. The three authorities play an important role in the development of the Jewar airport region and industrial investment. Through the reshuffle, the government has indicated its intention to speed up work in these areas.

stories.title: Fire breaks out at cotton and mattress shop in Gorakhpur:People flee screaming in Mohaddipur; police rescue children in their arms
stories.summary: A fire broke out at a cotton-and-mattress shop in Mohaddipur, Gorakhpur, late on Friday night, triggering panic. Screams began coming from the houses around the site, and people kept fleeing to safety. Meanwhile, Cantonment police took children trapped inside houses to a safe place. Four fire engines arrived 20 minutes after the incident. Firefighters brought the blaze under control after battling it for nearly two hours. No one was killed in the incident. According to police, Mohammad Owaisi owns the cotton-and-mattress shop at the Mohaddipur crossing in the Cantonment area. It is reported that the cotton caught fire at around 1 a.m. late on Friday night because of a short circuit. The fire then began spreading to nearby areas. Seeing the blaze take a terrifying form, people ran out of their houses screaming. Cantonment police reached the site immediately and took the children of the family to safety. A fire brigade team arrived after being informed. The fire was brought under control after two hours of strenuous efforts.

stories.summary: Varanasi's Tulsi Ghat witnessed the 500-year-old Nag Nathaiya Leela on Friday, recreating a scene from the Dwapar Yuga. During the traditional performance, a child dressed as Lord Krishna jumped into the Ganga from a 20-foot-high Kadamba tree. He then appeared seated on the hood of the serpent Kaliya, playing his flute. Large crowds gathered to watch the spectacle from the ghat steps, nearby buildings and boats. stories.title: Congress seeks maximum 68 seats in western UP:Party seeks to consolidate Dalit-Muslim support; will SP give up its 22 sitting seats?
stories.summary: The Congress has staked a claim to 181 seats ahead of the start of seat-sharing talks with the Samajwadi Party. The party has shown the greatest interest in seats in western Uttar Pradesh, where it has demanded 68 constituencies. This indicates that Congress wants to win back its traditional core voters, Muslims and Dalits. Since 2014, western Uttar Pradesh has largely remained a BJP stronghold. Before the BSP emerged as their main political choice, the Jatav community, the largest Dalit sub-group by population, used to be a committed Congress vote bank. The question is whether the SP will give up 22 seats it currently holds to accommodate an alliance with Congress. Congress has also staked a claim to 12 seats held by the RLD and SBSP, both of which were allies of the SP in 2022. How many seats will the parties be able to agree on in the meeting? Read the report... The Congress list of 181 Assembly seats includes 22 constituencies won by the SP in 2022. Of these, 19 are general-category seats and three are reserved seats. However, it is also true that the political equations have changed in six of these 22 constituencies since 2022. The BJP and its ally Apna Dal (S) wrested Muslim-dominated seats such as Kundarki, Katehari and Suar from the SP in by-elections. Manoj Pandey from Unchahar, Rakesh Singh from Gauriganj and Pooja Pal from Chail have also left the SP and joined the BJP. Will the SP give up the 22 seats it currently holds? According to senior journalist Yogesh Mishra, parties often have to compromise even on seats held by their sitting MLAs when forming an alliance. Of the 181 seats claimed by Congress, 22 were won by the SP in the 2022 elections. These include Bachhrawan, Sareni, Harchandpur and Unchahar in Rae Bareli; Chail in Kaushambi; Kalpi in Jalaun; and Katehari in Ambedkar Nagar. By-elections were subsequently held in Katehari and Kundarki. Meanwhile, leaders such as Manoj Pandey, the MLA from Unchahar, and Pooja Pal, the MLA from Chail, left the SP and joined the BJP. As a result, the SP now has sitting MLAs in only 16 of these 22 constituencies. However, the party remains strong in these seats. If Congress does not withdraw its claim to them, one possible compromise could be for the SP to field its MLAs on Congress tickets. Why has Congress demanded the highest number of seats in western UP? A regional breakdown of Congress's list of 181 Assembly seats shows that it wants to contest the highest number, 68, in western UP, followed by 65 in eastern UP, 34 in central UP and 14 in Bundelkhand. Of the 126 seats in western UP, the BJP won 85 in 2022, while the SP-RLD alliance won 41. The SP alliance swept Shamli and Moradabad. It also gave the BJP a tough fight in Muzaffarnagar and Meerut, while the BJP dominated other districts. At the time, the BSP's core voters were seen as leaning towards the BJP. However, a shift was visible in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. The SP-Congress alliance performed well in this belt with the support of Dalit voters. One reason cited for this was that Congress helped bring Dalit votes to the alliance. Congress firebrand leader Imran Masood also managed to win from western UP. He is currently the party's working president. Congress now wants to rebuild its roots in Uttar Pradesh by relying on its traditional core vote bank and the Dalit-Muslim equation in this region. The largest share of the Dalit vote bank is still associated with the BSP. However, Chandrashekhar is also preparing to make inroads into it this time. Congress is trying to establish the narrative that if the BJP has to be defeated, Dalits and Muslims should put their faith in it rather than looking elsewhere. In which regions of UP has Congress demanded more seats? Congress has staked its biggest claims in Assembly constituencies falling under the areas represented by its six sitting MPs. It has also included constituencies under Lok Sabha constituencies that were once its strongholds, including Maharajganj, Kushinagar, Bansgaon, Prayagraj, Varanasi, Kanpur, Jhansi, Sitapur, Rae Bareli, Amethi and Barabanki. The list also includes 39 Assembly constituencies where Congress was leading during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. How many seats will the SP and Congress agree on? Senior journalist Ratanmani Lal says that the biggest weakness of Congress is its organisation. It will need the SP's organisational strength to perform well. In 2017, when the SP contested the elections while in power, it gave Congress 104 seats. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the SP gave Congress 17 seats. At the rate of five Assembly constituencies per Lok Sabha constituency, this works out to 85 Assembly seats. This means that the seat-sharing arrangement between the SP and Congress is likely to be limited to 85 to 104 seats. This number would also be ideal for Congress. In 2022, it contested 399 seats but secured only 2.33% of the vote and won two seats. However, its vote share crossed 9% in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections after it joined hands with the SP. This was one of the factors that caused the NDA its biggest setback in Uttar Pradesh. If the two parties manage to coordinate effectively, Congress could also benefit in terms of vote share and seats in 2027. Congress has entrusted Priyanka with responsibility for seat-sharing talks Congress has formed a five-member committee to hold seat-sharing talks with the SP. Priyanka Gandhi will lead the committee. Its other members are KC Venugopal, UP in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam, state Congress president Aradhana Mishra and working president Imran Masood. The SP will be represented in the talks by leaders such as Akhilesh Yadav and Ram Gopal Yadav. According to senior sources in both parties, the final round of talks and the decision on seat-sharing will take place at a joint meeting of Mallikarjun Kharge, Rahul Gandhi and Akhilesh Yadav. Both parties are trying to resolve the seat-sharing issue by 30 November. Congress is set to begin its election campaign in Uttar Pradesh from 10 December.

stories.title: Who benefits if caste dominates UP elections?:BJP, which lost 29 seats in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls, wants to fight on Hindutva
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh politics once again appears to be revolving around the divide between caste and Hindutva. This time, the real battle is not about candidates but about deciding the key election issue. The Samajwadi Party-Congress alliance has already made it clear that it will fight the 2027 Assembly elections on the issue of caste. If this happens, the BJP could face greater losses. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the SP-Congress alliance gained 37 seats in Uttar Pradesh by raising concerns over the Constitution being under threat and using the PDA factor. The SP's vote share also increased by 15.48 percentage points. The Opposition wants to contest the next election using the same successful formula. On the other hand, statements by the BJP's top leadership, including Union Home Minister Amit Shah and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, make it clear that the party is preparing to take the election beyond caste divisions and fight on the agenda of Hindutva, nationalism, law and order, and the Uniform Civil Code. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the SP-Congress alliance won 43 of Uttar Pradesh's 80 seats with the help of the 'PDA' formula. The BJP, which had won 62 seats in 2019, was reduced to 33. This caste arithmetic also kept the BJP away from the majority mark of 272 seats in the Lok Sabha on its own. The Opposition is preparing to repeat a similar strategy in 2027, which is why Akhilesh Yadav is bringing the election closer to caste-based equations. Rallied support in Agra by calling Dalits 'powerful' On 15 November 2026, Akhilesh Yadav held a major 'Dalit Mahasammelan' in Agra. According to political observers, Dalit-dominated constituencies in western Uttar Pradesh have traditionally been considered strongholds of the BSP. Choosing Agra, a reserved constituency, Akhilesh gave a new meaning to the letter 'D' in the PDA formula, calling it 'Dumdaar Dalit' (powerful Dalit). He said that if his party came to power, it would provide a special package for the Dalit community. He also raised the issues of protecting reservation and the Constitution. Akhilesh makes a calculated move on the 'Social Transformation Front' On 12 November 2026, Asaduddin Owaisi (AIMIM) and Chandrashekhar Azad (Azad Samaj Party) announced the formation of the 'Social Transformation Front'. Instead of directly opposing the new alliance, which is focused on the Dalit-Muslim equation, Akhilesh welcomed it. Akhilesh claimed that the front would reduce the BJP's vote share by 2 to 3%. However, he also made it clear that the 'PDA' remained the biggest option for defeating the BJP. Political analysts believe that Akhilesh's stance is part of his strategy to win over Dalit and Muslim voters. Building ties with non-Yadav OBC and Dalit leaders To make up for the Jat vote in western Uttar Pradesh, the SP leadership has adopted a softer stance towards Chandrashekhar Azad, chief of the Azad Samaj Party. Party leaders have been asked not to attack him directly. In addition, the SP is working on a strategy to move beyond its traditional Muslim-Yadav (MY) base and give priority to non-Yadav backward castes in its organisation and ticket distribution. Akhilesh keeps expanding the meaning of PDA Akhilesh is not limiting the PDA formula to Yadavs, Muslims and Dalits. To strengthen caste-based mobilisation, he has expanded the meanings of its letters. He has said that 'P' stands for 'Pandit', while 'A' can mean 'Agra', 'Aadhi Aabadi' (women), 'Agarwal', 'Adivasi' and 'Annadata' (farmers). The strategy is aimed at making inroads into the BJP's core vote bank. Akhilesh is also planning visits to Ayodhya's Shri Ram Temple and Mathura in December to challenge the BJP on the issue of Hindutva. What is the BJP doing to counter this? Yogi and Shah's counter: 'No curfew, no riots' The BJP's top leadership began preparing its counter to caste-based politics as early as July 2024. The party's brainstorming meeting, being held in Mathura on 16 and 17 November, is also discussing how to shift the election focus away from caste and towards Hindutva, nationalism and law and order. Slogans convey a message of unity Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's slogan, "If we are divided, we will be cut down; if we stay united, we will remain strong", and Prime Minister Narendra Modi's slogan, "If we are united, we are safe", have set the tone for preventing the division of Hindu votes. The RSS is also working to take this campaign to the ground. Major UCC move Union Home Minister Amit Shah has made it clear at a state executive committee meeting that the Uniform Civil Code will be implemented in Uttar Pradesh if the BJP forms the government for a third consecutive term. Yogi's aggressive Hindutva pitch In his speeches, Chief Minister Yogi has adopted an aggressive stance, recalling the riots and alleged appeasement during the SP's rule. His key statements have raised the political temperature: According to senior journalist and political analyst Akhilesh Bajpai, caste equations have always played a decisive role in Uttar Pradesh politics. Whenever elections in the state have been fought on caste lines, the Hindutva card has weakened. The 1993 Assembly elections offer an example. After the Babri structure was demolished in 1992, the Hindutva wave was at its peak across northern India. However, in the 1993 Assembly elections, the SP-BSP alliance mobilised voters along caste lines with the slogan, 'Mulayam and Kanshi Ram have joined hands; Jai Shri Ram has been blown away', and formed a government with a clear majority. On the other hand, SP national president Akhilesh Yadav is also preparing to counter this strategy by inaugurating the Kedareshwar Temple in Etawah before the elections. After that, he will visit Ayodhya to seek the blessings of Ram Lalla, in an attempt to balance the issues being raised by the Opposition camp. Senior journalist Yogesh Kumar says that even after its defeat in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the BJP's central leadership has not yet made it clear that it will not make Hindutva an election issue. This is because the political narrative has to be set in Delhi. The BJP, too, is forming alliances with caste-based political parties. The RLD, SBSP, Apna Dal (S) and Nishad Party are all caste-based parties.

stories.title: Youth jumps into Gomti after girlfriend's marriage condition:She said he must earn ₹50,000 to marry her, he made a final call to friend in Jaunpur
stories.summary: A young man jumped into the Gomti River in Jaunpur after hearing his girlfriend's condition. The girl had said, "Earn ₹50,000 a month, and only then will I marry you. Otherwise, I will marry someone else." Divers have been searching for the young man for more than 18 hours. His brother has accused a girl from the city of blackmailing him. His brother said, "The two had been having an affair for about a year. At around 12 midnight on Sunday, my younger brother jumped into the river." The incident took place at Shahi Bridge in the Kotwali police station area. Read the full incident in sequence… Rahit Maurya (45) lives with his family in Gopalapur village under the Saraikhwaja police station. His family consists of his wife, Anju Maurya (42), three sons-Satyam Maurya (26), Shivam Maurya (22) and Sundaram Maurya (20)-and a daughter, Kajal (19). Rahit is a post office agent. His elder brother Shivam is married and works as a contractor at a brick kiln. His younger brother Shivam works in land plotting, while Sundaram was a third-year BA student. He video-called a friend and said, "I am going to jump" Sundaram left home at around 9 p.m. on Sunday night. He reached Shahi Bridge, 3 km away, at around midnight. From there, he video-called his friend, Praveen Maurya, and said, "I am going to jump into the Gomti. Tell my family." He hung up after saying this. After receiving the information from his friend, the family rushed to the spot. They immediately called the police as well. The police and divers had been searching for Sundaram since Monday morning. However, even after more than 18 hours, no trace of him could be found. Father says girl used to blackmail his son Sundaram's father, Rahit Maurya, said, "Sundaram had been having an affair for about a year with Naina, a constable's daughter. She used to harass him and pressure him to earn money. My son jumped from Shahi Bridge." The girl used to say, "Earn ₹50,000 a month" Sundaram's brother, Shivam Maurya, said, “A girl named Naina had been harassing my brother for several days. She told him, 'I will marry you only if you earn ₹50,000.'” My brother would tell me, my father and several others every day, "Brother, if you know of any work, please help me get it." City CO Samyak Chaudhary said- The initial investigation suggests that the case is related to a love affair. The complaint has been received. The investigation is underway, and the young man is also being searched for with the help of divers.

stories.title: BJP MLA Chandrabhanu Paswan injured in Ayodhya road accident:Fortuner collides with trailer, suffers serious head injury
stories.summary: Milkipur MLA Chandrabhanu Paswan was injured after his Fortuner car collided with a trailer in Ayodhya. The accident took place near Bhambhwa crossing in Rani Bazar, under the Poorakalandar police station area. Paswan suffered a head injury and was taken to the district hospital for treatment. The cause of the accident is not yet known. District Magistrate Shashank Tripathi reached the district hospital and spoke to officials to get details about the MLA's condition. Police have started efforts to trace the trailer and its driver. See three pictures below : Now read the full account विधायक Chandrabhanu Paswan was on his way to attend the Bharatkund festival. At 8:30 p.m., a trailer travelling from Prabhat Nagar towards Shahganj near Bhanbhawa Crossing in Ranibazar, under the jurisdiction of Purakalandar police station, collided violently with his Fortuner car. The collision struck the side of the car where the MLA was seated. The MLA suffered injuries to his head and leg in the accident. He was admitted to the district hospital after his head began bleeding, and is undergoing treatment there. According to eyewitnesses, the collision was so forceful that the MLA's Fortuner was damaged. After the accident, people ran to stop the trailer, but the driver increased the vehicle's speed and fled the scene. Driver's side used to get him out when gate would not open After the accident, the Fortuner's gate would not open. The MLA was therefore taken out through the driver's side. He was bleeding from the head and had also suffered an injury to his leg. He was then immediately taken to the district hospital. Following information about the incident, Ayodhya District Magistrate and the CO City reached the spot. Police are gathering information about the accident. A search is under way for the trailer and its driver. The MLA's condition is said to be out of danger. As soon as news of the incident spread, BJP leaders, workers and the MLA's supporters began arriving at the district hospital. District officials also reached the hospital and are gathering information about the MLA's health. While gathering information about the accident, police have begun efforts to trace the trailer and its driver. The cause of the accident is being investigated. Traffic around the crossroads was also affected for some time after the accident. Police restored normal conditions at the scene. Victory came in the February 2025 by-election Chandrabhanu Paswan defeated Samajwadi Party candidate Ajit Prasad by 61,710 votes in the by-election for the Milkipur Assembly seat. Paswan received 1,46,397 votes, while Ajit Prasad received 84,687 votes. Ajit Prasad is the son of Awadhesh Prasad, the Samajwadi Party MP from Faizabad. The Milkipur Assembly seat fell vacant after Awadhesh Prasad won the 2024 Lok Sabha election from the Faizabad seat. Notably, in the 2022 Assembly election, Milkipur was the only seat in Ayodhya district where the BJP was defeated. The story is being updated.

stories.title: Soldier dies after being shot 8 days before wedding:Was posted in Kupwara; father says two bullets hit his head
stories.summary: An Army soldier from Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh, died after being shot while on duty in Kupwara, Jammu and Kashmir, on Sunday evening. He was hit by two bullets in the head. The Army informed his family about his death at around 7 am on Monday. The news left the family members in tears. The soldier was due to get married on November 24, while his engagement ceremony was scheduled for November 22. The wedding invitations had already been distributed, and preparations were underway to welcome guests at home. The family had been waiting for the soldier to return home on Monday. Now, they are waiting for his body to arrive at the same house. However, the circumstances in which the soldier died and how he was shot are not yet known. Karan joined the Army in 2020, was posted in Kupwara Pappu Singh, a resident of Sirsa village in the Chharra police station area, works in agriculture. Karan was the youngest of his three children. His elder brother, Sanjay Chaudhary, is also an Army soldier, while his sister is married. Karan Chaudhary, 25, joined the Army in 2020. After completing his training in Ranchi, he was posted to the Leh Glacier for his first assignment. He was later posted to Lohlam in Kupwara, Jammu and Kashmir, for his second and third assignments. He was serving with the 22 Rashtriya Rifles (RR) Battalion. Family members said they had spoken to Karan on 14 November. He told them that he would take a flight from Srinagar on 16 November and reach Delhi. He planned to travel to the village from there. He was also due to receive leave-related documents from the headquarters. Death caused by two bullets to the head; reason unclear His father, Pappu Singh, said the battalion's commanding officer informed him of Karan's death at around 7 a.m. on Monday. He was told that Karan had suffered two bullet wounds to the head. However, no information was provided about how he was shot. The family was only informed that their son had been martyred. As soon as they heard the news of his death, panic swept through the family. His relatives began crying inconsolably. The family is demanding that the Army headquarters and officials clarify the cause of his death. Engagement on 22 November, wedding scheduled for 24 November The father said that preparations for Karan's wedding were almost complete. The match was arranged in April after the girl was shown to the family over a video call. A family meeting and engagement were scheduled to take place in the village on 22 November, while the wedding procession was to depart from a guest house in Atrauli on 24 November. The wedding invitations had been distributed. Preparations for the clothes, other items and decorations had also been completed. Relatives had begun visiting the family. They had hoped that Karan would return home and take part in the wedding preparations. But the house from which the wedding procession was to leave eight days later is now filled with mourning. Body to be brought to Delhi tonight after post-mortem According to information, Karan's body will be brought to Delhi tonight after the post-mortem. It is likely to reach his village, Sirsa, by Tuesday morning. However, the official confirmation of the final timing has not yet been received. Ataruli SDM Saurabh Kumar Gupta said he was informed of the soldier's death on Monday morning. The administration has not yet received the official time for the body to reach the village. Further information will be provided once an update is received. Preparations to welcome athlete Gulveer Singh also affected Sirsa is also the village of international athlete Gulveer Singh. Preparations had been under way for Gulveer's arrival in the village and his welcome. The villagers were excited, but news of Karan's death plunged the entire village into mourning. The villagers are now waiting for the mortal remains of their young son to reach the village.
