stories.title: Azam Khan on Yogi's mother:'This is a great shock'; says no one has wealth like a mother; supporters chant 'the lion has arrived' as he reaches Moradabad
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan reached Moradabad with his son, Abdullah Azam, late on Friday evening. There, he expressed grief over the death of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's mother. Azam said, "It is a great shock. May Allah grant her patience. It is a great loss; no one possesses a treasure like a mother." Supporters welcomed Azam on his arrival in Moradabad and raised slogans. They said, "Look, look who has arrived-the lion has arrived, the lion has arrived." Azam Khan waved his hand and asked them not to raise slogans. He said he had not come to engage in politics. After this, Azam Khan reached Gulab Mosque in Harthala and offered prayers. Azam visits SP leader Yusuf Malik's home After offering prayers, Azam Khan reached the home of his close associate and SP leader Yusuf Malik. There, he expressed grief over the death of Yusuf Malik's son. He then went to the cemetery and visited his son's grave. Yusuf Malik was held with Azam Khan in Rampur jail for a long time. During that period, police arrested him on charges of threatening to kill and attacking the Additional Municipal Commissioner of Moradabad. He was later also booked under the National Security Act (NSA). Azam Khan released from jail after a year Azam Khan reached Rampur at around 10 p.m. on Wednesday after being released from jail. There, he had said, "There will be no election; there will be a revolution. There will be no change; there will be a flood. The ED officials should repair their image and reform themselves. They should neither ruin the country nor themselves." Earlier, as soon as Azam came out of Dasna jail in Ghaziabad, supporters and the media surrounded him. Azam remained silent, then said only this: "I stand by what I have always said. A Muslim built the temple of education; this is his punishment." Find out which case led the ED to arrest Azam Read what happened after Azam was released from jail On 29 October, the High Court suspended the 10-year sentences handed down to Azam and his son Abdullah in the two PAN card cases and granted them bail. Both were subsequently released from Rampur jail. Azam walked out of Rampur jail on the evening of 31 October, after 11 months in custody. Just 15 minutes later, the ED arrested him in the money laundering case and took him to Ghaziabad. The ED's special PMLA court first sent Azam to judicial custody until 14 November and then extended it until 26 November.

stories.title: Dhirendra Shastri holds court with people claiming to be possessed:Women roll on ground, men tear clothes while grinding teeth at Raja Bhaiya's event
stories.summary: Dhirendra Shastri's divine court was held in Pratapgarh on Friday. Slips bearing the names of devotees were drawn. During the event, he said, "Those suffering from spirit-related ailments should come forward." After this, women and men from all three marquees went near the stage. As soon as Dhirendra Shastri began reciting the Hanuman Chalisa, some people started screaming and shouting. Several women began rolling on the ground and swaying. One young man began beating his head, while another performed a snake dance. Some men were seen gnashing their teeth. One young man tore his shirt and began beating his chest. At the court, Dhirendra Shastri said, "If miracles could be performed merely with sacred ash, why would he have a cancer hospital built?" He cited the example of Lord Hanuman bringing the Sanjeevani herb and saving Lakshman's life. He said people should not stop taking medicines after getting caught up in such gatherings. After the divine court, Dhirendra Shastri jumped off the stage and climbed down. He met Raja Bhaiya and took his leave. Raja Bhaiya himself drove him to the helicopter. Earlier, Raja Bhaiya explained why he drove Dhirendra Shastri himself from Prayagraj to Pratapgarh. He said, "If we wanted, we could have brought Bageshwar Dham Sarkar here from Prayag by helicopter. But we wanted to see who would try to stop us, which is why I went there myself. I did not see anyone on the way." Earlier, a three-day Ram Katha was held at Raja Bhaiya's residence in Benti from 17 to 19 November. Several ministers in the Uttar Pradesh government, film actors and several VIPs attended it. Strongman leaders Brij Bhushan Singh, Brijesh Singh and Dhananjay Singh also attended the religious discourse.

stories.title: Woman employee beats XEN inside his office in Hamirpur:Says he holds her hand and asks for her address, asks when she will treat him to tea
stories.summary: In Hamirpur, a woman employee of the electricity department severely beat the XEN in his cabin. The woman alleges that the XEN behaved indecently towards her. She said he called her into his cabin, held her hand and asked for her home address. When the woman beat the XEN, the other office staff continued to support her. A video of the incident has also emerged. The XEN was heard saying only, "This is wrong." The woman, who has filed a written complaint with the police, has demanded action. The matter falls under the jurisdiction of the Nagar Kotwali police station. First, look at the two pictures... Now read the full matter... Manoj Kumar Vishwakarma is posted as an executive engineer (XEN) in the Electricity Testing Division. A woman works there as an executive assistant. The woman said that after her husband's death, she lived alone in a rented room. Manoj often behaved inappropriately around her. He asked her over the phone for the address of her room. On Friday, Manoj Kumar called her to his chamber and asked, "When are you inviting me to your home for tea?" She told him that if he wanted tea from her home, they could order it there and he could have tea in the chamber, but that she would not invite him to her home. After this, he grabbed her hand and pulled her towards him. He would call her to his cabin In response, I beat him. By what right did he hold my hand? If he is the boss, he should behave like one. Earlier too, he would call me to his cabin. There, he would keep talking about one pointless thing or another. He would hold my hand and say, "Your line is very long; someone will support you." I told the other people in the office about it as well. Everyone went with me to the cabin. I asked him why he had held her hand, but he began making false excuses. I then beat him in anger. Office staff also strongly criticised him It may be noted that a video of the assault has emerged, showing a heated argument taking place inside the office. Other office staff also berated the executive engineer, accusing him of holding the female employee's hand and inviting her home for tea. They said he should be ashamed of holding the hand of a woman who was the same age as his daughter. When the executive engineer tried to offer an explanation, the victim slapped him. Woman says- Pressure is being exerted to reach a settlement The woman says that pressure is being exerted on her to reach a settlement in the case. Robbie Gautam, the assistant engineer in the meter department, has also been calling her repeatedly. She has been frightened since the incident. She fears that the accused may enter her rented house one day and do something untoward. She has filed a complaint with the police and sought protection. XEN says- I have been wronged Meanwhile, XEN Manoj Kumar said that false allegations had been levelled against him. "After being so humiliated, I am sitting before you. If I were a thief or a criminal, or had done anything wrong, I would not be sitting before you; I would have left. I am sitting here because I have been wronged-I have not wronged anyone. When I asked them to do the work, they beat me and filmed me." Kotwali in-charge Ramakant Shukla said The female employee has submitted a written complaint. We have sent a team to the spot. Further action will be taken after the investigation.

stories.title: '₹15,000 crore scam in Jal Jeevan Mission':Sanjay Singh says tanks are collapsing, blacklisted firms getting tenders; government shielding them
stories.summary: Aam Aadmi Party Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh has alleged corruption amounting to ₹15,000 crore in work carried out under the Jal Jeevan Mission in Uttar Pradesh. He said government funds had been looted in the name of a scheme to supply water to villages. Around ₹15,000 crore had been withdrawn without any work being carried out. Questioning the department's Principal Secretary, Anurag Srivastava, and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Sanjay Singh said officials involved in corruption were being protected. He also said central investigative agencies were silent on the matter. Sanjay Singh referred to water tanks collapsing in Kasganj, Bareilly, Sitapur and Basti. He alleged a scam in the name of excavation and accused officials of purchasing materials from blacklisted companies. He also questioned how the company that built the tank in Bareilly received a tender worth crores of rupees in Hyderabad. Questions raised over company that donated ₹60 crore to BJP Referring to Nagarjuna Construction Company, Sanjay Singh alleged that the company had donated ₹60 crore to the BJP. He questioned how the company was continuing to receive tenders despite allegations of corruption. He also questioned the role of the Enforcement Directorate. He claimed that on 14 September, the ED had sought a report related to corruption from the department, but no action had been taken so far. He asked why the investigation against the company had not progressed. Government cornered over Gorakhpur incident At the press conference, Sanjay Singh referred to the Gorakhpur incident and expressed his condolences to the victim's family. He alleged that Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath was trying to provoke the family in the matter. The MP also accused the government of alleging murder without an investigation and politicising the accident. He said that Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav had released CCTV footage related to the incident and expressed his condolences to the victims. Asked about accident involving CM's convoy: What action was taken? Sanjay Singh raised the issue of the accident involving Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's convoy in Arjunganj, Lucknow. He claimed that a mother and her son had died in the accident. He questioned what action had been taken in the case so far. He alleged that no action is taken in cases involving people linked to the BJP, while the police take immediate action in other cases. Also alleges cases and pressure The AAP MP said that Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath had several cases registered against him. He alleged that the owner of the house where his office is located had also been intimidated and threatened. Sanjay Singh said that those who criticise the government are being targeted.

stories.title: Azam Khan offers Friday prayers with son Abdullah:Says, ‘There is no major issue to talk about’
stories.summary: Azam Khan went to the mosque near his home in Rampur today, Friday, to offer Jumu'ah prayers along with his son, Abdullah Azam, and several associates. He left home at 1:07 p.m. and entered the mosque at around 1:10 p.m. After offering prayers for around 10 minutes, he came out at 1:21 p.m. Two minutes later, Azam Khan and Abdullah Azam reached home. Spoke to media, said, "We spoke at length yesterday" As he came out of the mosque, Azam Khan told media personnel, "We spoke to you at length yesterday. There is no such major issue to discuss." He then went inside the house. People continued to arrive at the house to meet him. Supporters have been arriving in large numbers since his release Azam Khan reached his home at around 9:40 p.m. on Wednesday night after being released from Ghaziabad's Dasna jail. Thousands of supporters and well-wishers arrived to meet him. The stream of people arriving and meeting him continued until around 2 a.m. People continued to arrive to meet him from 10 a.m. on Thursday until 11 p.m. People have been arriving at his residence since Friday morning. Many have already met him, while a large number of people are waiting for their turn. Supporters who have come from distant places are asking about his well-being and also telling him about their problems. Azam Khan is meeting them and enquiring about their well-being. Spent 2.5 hours at Jauhar University as well Azam Khan had also arrived at his dream project, Mohammad Ali Jauhar University, on Thursday night. He spent around 2.5 hours there and took stock of the situation on the campus by speaking to employees and administrative officials. Meetings continued at his residence on Friday even after the Friday prayers. The police also appeared alert regarding security arrangements.

stories.title: Yogi went to his mother’s door seeking alms:She broke down upon seeing him in saffron robes and asked, ‘What was lacking at home?’
stories.summary: Her son, who had been missing for three years, was returning home. His mother was overjoyed on hearing the news. She had several questions running through her mind. How would her son look? What was he doing? She went to the door, but froze at the sight before her. The son she had last seen leaving home in jeans and trousers was now standing in saffron robes. His head was shaved, he wore large earrings in both ears and held a begging bowl in his hand. He had not come for an ordinary meeting. He had come to seek alms from his own mother. This son was none other than the present-day Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. At the time, his name was Ajay Singh Bisht and he had become a monk. Standing before his mother, he said just one thing: “Mother, please give me alms.” Senior journalist Vijay Trivedi has described this emotional incident in his book Yada Yada Hi Yogi. According to him, Ajay arrived outside his house and called out for alms. Hearing the voice, the woman of the house came to the door but could not believe her eyes. Her mouth fell open, but no words came out. Here is what happened next. Mother asked, ‘What was lacking at home that you are begging?’ His mother was unable to understand what she was seeing. Ajay then said, “Mother, please give me alms.” Gathering herself, she asked, “Son, what have you done to yourself? What was lacking at home that you have to beg?” Ajay replied, “Mother, renunciation is my duty. A yogi can satisfy his hunger only through alms. Whatever you give me will help fulfil my purpose.” His mother still hoped that he would come inside the house. She said, “Son, come inside first.” But Ajay firmly refused. He said, “No, Mother. I cannot enter the house or leave this place without receiving alms. Whatever you can give me, please do so. Only then will I leave.” His mother eventually gave in to his insistence. She went inside and brought some rice and money, placing them in Ajay’s bowl. As soon as he received the alms, Ajay turned around and walked away. His mother stood at the doorway with tears in her eyes, watching her son leave. Vijay Trivedi has described the incident in an emotional manner in his book. In his words, as soon as Yogi received the alms, he walked away. His voice echoed towards the clouds gathering near the mountains as he chanted, “Alakh Niranjan!” The sun appeared to be hiding behind the clouds and moving towards the mountains. Its light had become meaningless for the mother. Father searched for six months before learning that his son was in Gorakhpur Yogi Adityanath’s childhood name was Ajay Singh Bisht. He completed his intermediate education in 1989 from Bharat Mandir Inter College in Rishikesh. In the same year, he enrolled for a BSc course at Dr Pitambar Datt Barthwal Himalayan Government Postgraduate College in Kotdwar, Pauri. He completed his studies there in 1992. After this, he enrolled for an MSc in Physics at Gorakhpur University but did not complete the course. It was during this period that he left home. For nearly six months, his family had no idea where Ajay was. His father, Anand Singh Bisht, searched for him everywhere he thought his son might be. However, he could not find him. Later, someone informed the family that Ajay was at the Gorakhnath Peeth in Gorakhpur and had become a monk. The news deeply saddened his father. He wanted to bring his son back home, but Ajay was firm about his decision. Declared successor to Gorakshapeeth on February 15, 1994 Ajay had chosen the path of renunciation. On February 15, 1994, Gorakshapeethadhishwar Mahant Avaidyanath formally declared him his successor following the prescribed rituals. After this, the purpose of his life changed. Away from family and domestic life, he dedicated himself to the Gorakshapeeth and service to society. The same Ajay later became Yogi Adityanath. He was first elected as the MP from Gorakhpur in 1998 and went on to win five consecutive Lok Sabha elections. In 2017, he became the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh. Mahant Avaidyanath had reportedly told the family, “You have four sons. Give one of them to us.” The decision was not easy for Yogi’s mother. She kept looking first at Mahant Avaidyanath and then at her son. Eventually, she returned home with her husband. Yogi remained firm on his decision to become a monk Yogi Adityanath faced several challenges in his monastic life but remained committed to his decision. On February 15, 1994, Gorakshapeethadhishwar Mahant Avaidyanath formally declared him his successor following the prescribed rituals. Yogi Adityanath later expressed the purpose of his life through the following Sanskrit verse: Na Tvam Kamayé Rajyam, Na Swargam Na Punarbhavam. Kamayé Duhkh-Taptanam Praninam Arti-Nashanam. Its meaning is: “O Lord, I do not seek power, heaven or liberation. My only wish is to relieve the suffering of living beings who are afflicted by pain.” Yogi Adityanath was first elected as the MP from Gorakhpur in 1998. He went on to win five consecutive Lok Sabha elections and became the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh in 2017. Even after entering politics, he remained in touch with his family and continued to meet his mother, Savitri Devi. In May 2022, nearly five years after becoming Chief Minister, he visited his native village. He touched his mother’s feet to seek her blessings and asked her, “You recognised me, didn’t you?” He also visited her at AIIMS Rishikesh in June 2024 when she was admitted there. He met her again on February 9, 2026. Following his mother’s death, Yogi Adityanath may once again visit his ancestral village of Panchur. This time, however, his mother will not be waiting for him at the doorstep.

stories.title: Officer informs Yogi of mother's death:Remains composed on stage in Gorakhpur; completes programme before leaving for temple
stories.summary: When the tragic news of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's mother's death arrived, he was addressing a tablet distribution programme in Gorakhpur. Former IAS officer Awanish Awasthi and MP Ravi Kishan, who were present on the stage, shared the news with each other. They began waiting for the Chief Minister to finish his address. He spoke for around 61 minutes. After finishing his speech, he turned around and found Awanish Awasthi behind him. Awasthi whispered something in his ear. It is believed that Awasthi informed him of his mother's death. His facial expression changed for a few moments. However, he did not make his personal grief public. He concluded the programme, took selfies with the children and then left for the temple. He subsequently departed from Gorakhpur for Uttarakhand. This was not the first time in Yogi's life that he had prioritised his public responsibilities amid personal grief. Earlier, in 2020, his father, Anand Singh Bisht, died during the coronavirus pandemic. At that time too, he prioritised his responsibilities as Chief Minister. He could not attend his father's last rites. At the time, Yogi had said that wherever his father might be, he would be blessing him. He had said that his father would also have wished for his son to serve the people of the country and the state. Even at such a time, he gave priority to the concerns of nearly 25 crore people of the state over those of his family. Ravi Kishan paid tribute during the programme Gorakhpur MP Ravi Kishan was also present at the tablet distribution programme. During the event, he shared the news of Savitri Devi's death on social media and paid a heartfelt tribute to her. Despite this, the Chief Minister completed his address and proceeded according to the scheduled programme. When he left home, his mother thought he was going away for a job Yogi Adityanath's original name is Ajay Singh Bisht. When he decided to leave home in 1993, his family thought he was going away for work. The family later learnt that he had taken initiation into the Nath sect and become a monk. When he returned home for the first time after becoming a monk, his mother, Savitri Devi, tried to stop him. She also gave her son fruit, rice and money. However, seeing Ajay's resolve, his mother ultimately blessed him. When he returned to the village five years later, he asked his mother, "You recognised me, didn't you?" Even after becoming Chief Minister, Yogi Adityanath remained emotionally attached to his mother. After becoming Chief Minister for the second time on 3 May 2022, he visited his ancestral village, Panchur, after a gap of nearly five years. After touching his mother's feet to seek her blessings, he smiled and asked, "You recognised me, didn't you?" His mother also said that she recognised him. The meeting was highly emotional. In June 2024, Yogi Adityanath had also visited AIIMS Rishikesh to meet his mother. At the time, Savitri Devi was admitted to the hospital due to health-related problems. Yogi met her and enquired about her well-being. Attention also on whether he will attend the Prime Minister's programme Prime Minister Narendra Modi's programme is scheduled to be held in Lucknow on 21 November. It remains to be seen whether Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will attend it. However, people close to him claim that he may be present at the programme. After receiving news of his mother's death, he may travel today to Panchur, his ancestral village in Pauri Garhwal, Uttarakhand, to pay his last respects.

stories.title: BJP leader’s son killed by JCB, 5 arrested:SP leader questioned; family alleges police surrounded house
stories.summary: Police have arrested five people, including the JCB driver, in connection with the death of a BJP leader’s son in Gorakhpur. The arrests were made late on Thursday night. Police teams are conducting raids to trace other suspects. Samajwadi Party (SP) leader Sadhu Yadav was also brought from his home to the AIIMS police station for questioning. His family recorded a video of the police action and shared it on social media. Yadav has also been named as an accused in the FIR. Yadav’s wife, Chinta Yadav, had contested the Assembly election from the Campierganj constituency on an SP ticket. Sadhu Yadav is preparing to contest the upcoming Assembly election and has also applied to the party for a ticket. Family claims police surrounded the house Sadhu Yadav’s brother, Surendra Yadav, shared a video on social media in which he can be seen calling SP office-bearers to the house. In the video, he claims that police personnel had surrounded the house from all sides. However, SP City Nimish Patil said five accused had been arrested. They were identified as Vinod Shahi of Jhangha; Shivang Nishad and Nar Singh Yadav of Failaha village in Raghopatti, Chiluatala; Rahul Yadav of Bauliya Colony, who currently lives in Padri Bazaar, Shahpur; and Virendra Yadav of Gonarpura village in Rampur Gopalpur, Gulriha. Police said they were investigating all aspects of the case. Sadhu Yadav was being questioned, and investigators were trying to establish his role. Police have also seized four JCB machines. BJP leader’s son run over by bulldozer On Wednesday, four bulldozers were deployed during a roadshow in Gorakhpur to welcome Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav. A large floral garland was hung from one of them, while another carried a poster reading, ‘Akhilesh, Gen-Z’s favourite’. After the roadshow, 14-year-old Aryavardhan, son of BJP leader Omkar Singh, was run over by one of the bulldozers as it was returning. The driver abandoned the vehicle and fled. Police first seized the bulldozer involved in the accident and took possession of the other three on Thursday. An FIR has been registered against the driver, Sadhu Yadav and five other named accused, along with 60 unidentified people. Akhilesh was welcomed with a garland from a bulldozer The bulldozers had been decorated to welcome Akhilesh Yadav during the roadshow. One carried a large floral garland, while another displayed the poster describing him as ‘Gen-Z’s favourite’. Akhilesh was also welcomed with a garland presented from a bulldozer during the roadshow. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar after being named in the FIR, Sadhu Yadav denied arranging any JCB machines. He claimed that his name had been included in the FIR due to a misunderstanding. His wife had previously contested the Assembly election from the Campierganj seat. Sadhu Yadav has now sought an SP ticket to contest the upcoming election himself. Police seize all four bulldozers According to the AIIMS police, four bulldozers had been stationed on both sides of the main road at Kudaghat to welcome Akhilesh Yadav. The vehicle involved in the accident bears registration number UP-53-ET-6053. Police seized it on Wednesday and took it to the AIIMS police station. The remaining three bulldozers were also seized on Thursday. Police are now trying to identify their owners and establish who had arranged for the machines to be brought to the spot. The AIIMS police registered an FIR against the JCB driver, SP leader Sadhu Yadav alias Sadhu Bhaiya, Manoj Yadav, Mrityunjay Yadav alias Bittu, Yogesh Yadav, Chandra Prakash and 60 unidentified people. Aryavardhan was on his way to pick up his sister Aryavardhan’s father, Omkar Singh, said his son had left for a nearby crossing at around 2 pm on Wednesday to pick up his sister, Samriddhi. He was hit by a bulldozer returning from the roadshow. He was taken to AIIMS in a critical condition, where doctors declared him dead. SP City Nimish Patil said a bulldozer taking part in the SP roadshow collided with a motorcycle in the AIIMS police station area. The boy sustained serious injuries and was taken to hospital, where he was declared dead. Aryavardhan was a Class 10 student at Kendriya Vidyalaya, Nanda Nagar. His father, Omkar Singh, is the district co-convenor of the BJP’s Election Commission Liaison Department. Aryavardhan was on his way to pick up his sister Aryavardhan's father, Omkar Singh, said his son was on his way towards the crossroads at around 2 p.m. on Wednesday to pick up his sister, Samriddhi. During this time, he was hit by a bulldozer returning from a roadshow. He was taken to AIIMS in critical condition, where doctors declared him dead. City Superintendent of Police Nimish Patil said that a bulldozer taking part in the Samajwadi Party's roadshow in the AIIMS area collided with a motorcycle. stories.title: CM Yogi's mother Savitri Devi passes away at 91:Last rites to be held today, CM to leave for Uttarakhand
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath’s mother, Savitri Devi, died on Friday at the age of 91. She had been unwell for a long time. She breathed her last at her home in Panchur village in Pauri Garhwal district, Uttarakhand. SSP Sarvesh Pawar said her last rites may be performed at Sampoornanand Ghat in Rishikesh on Saturday. At the time of her death, Yogi Adityanath was addressing a programme titled Sashakt Yuva, Samriddh Uttar Pradesh (Empowered Youth, Prosperous Uttar Pradesh) in Gorakhpur. CM Pushkar Singh Dhami expresses condolences Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami paid tribute to Savitri Devi in a post on X. He wrote, A mother’s affection, blessings and love are among life’s most precious possessions. Her passing is an irreparable loss for the family. I pray to Baba Kedar to grant the departed soul a place at his feet and give Yogi ji and all the grieving family members the strength to bear this immense loss. Yogi was the fifth of seven children Yogi Adityanath was born into a Garhwali Rajput family. His father, Anand Singh Bisht, was a forest ranger, while his mother, Savitri Devi, was a homemaker. His father died on April 20, 2020. Yogi was the fifth of seven children. He has three elder sisters, an elder brother and two younger brothers. Mother raised the family in the village while her son became Gorakshpeeth Mahant After Ajay Singh Bisht, as Yogi Adityanath was originally named, renounced worldly life, his family continued living in Panchur village. Savitri Devi remained there with the family, while her other children took care of their respective lives and responsibilities. Meanwhile, Yogi became increasingly involved in the activities of Gorakhnath Temple. As a disciple of Mahant Avaidyanath, he took an active role in religious and social work. In 1998, he was elected to the Lok Sabha for the first time from Gorakhpur. He went on to win the seat five consecutive times and represented the constituency until 2014. After Mahant Avaidyanath’s death in 2014, Yogi became the head priest of Gorakshapeeth. On March 19, 2017, he took oath as the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh. Ajay Singh Bisht from Panchur village had thus become a prominent figure in national politics, but his meetings with his family and mother remained limited. Yogi could not attend his father’s last rites Yogi Adityanath’s father, Anand Singh Bisht, died on April 20, 2020, when the country was battling the Covid-19 pandemic. Yogi was serving as Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister and handling administrative responsibilities. He could not reach home to pay his last respects to his father. He had expressed regret over this, saying he had deeply wished to see his father one last time. His father’s last rites were performed in Haridwar. The incident once again brought attention to the distance between Yogi and his family. Yogi became emotional when he met his mother in 2022 May 3, 2022, was a special day for Yogi’s family. He visited his ancestral village, Panchur, after nearly five years. The visit was to attend his nephew’s mundan ceremony, a traditional head-shaving ritual. According to media reports, it was his first visit to Uttarakhand for a family function in around 28 years. On reaching home, Yogi touched his mother’s feet and sought her blessings. She blessed her son, and he presented her with a shawl. Savitri Devi became emotional during the meeting. Yogi shared a photograph of the meeting on social media with just one word: “Maa” (Mother). He also spent the night with his family in the village. It was reportedly his first night at his ancestral home in around 30 years. Yogi visited his mother at AIIMS Rishikesh in 2024 Savitri Devi’s health deteriorated in June 2024 due to age-related complications. She was admitted to AIIMS Rishikesh. On June 16, 2024, Yogi Adityanath visited her at the hospital. He spoke to doctors about her health and spent around 20 minutes with her. Uttarakhand Health Minister Dhan Singh Rawat and former Chief Minister Trivendra Singh Rawat were also present. The meeting drew attention as Yogi was seeing his mother after nearly two years. Before this, he had visited Panchur village in May 2022. During the visit, he also enquired about people from Uttar Pradesh who had been injured in a road accident in Rudraprayag. Yogi visited Panchur again in May 2026 In May 2026, Yogi Adityanath visited his ancestral village once again during a two-day trip to Uttarakhand. He attended the consecration ceremony of the Vishnu Panchdev Temple in Panchur and a Mahayagya. After the events, he visited his ancestral home and sought his mother Savitri Devi’s blessings. He spent time with his family, walked along the village paths and met local residents. Another emotional moment during the visit came when he paid floral tributes to a statue of his father, Anand Singh Bisht.

stories.title: Lawyer’s daughter dies in car-dumper collision:Truck hits car from behind, trapping 5 people, including her mother, after wedding trip
stories.summary: A 20-year-old woman, the daughter of a lawyer, died in a road accident in Lucknow while returning from a wedding ceremony with her mother and three neighbours. The group had gone to a resort for the wedding. Late on Thursday night, their car rammed into the rear of a dumper travelling ahead. A speeding truck coming from behind then hit the car, crushing it in the impact. Five occupants trapped inside car All five occupants were trapped inside the badly damaged car. Passers-by managed to open the door and rescue Sameeksha’s mother, Geeta, neighbour Shikhar, his wife Sukriti and his mother. They were taken to hospital for treatment. However, Sameeksha was trapped in the rear of the car and could not be rescued by the bystanders. After receiving information, police reached the spot and spent around one and a half hours trying to free her. She was eventually pulled out and taken to hospital, where doctors declared her dead. Worked with Jio in Mumbai Sameeksha worked with Jio in Mumbai. She had completed her MBA in Hyderabad and had returned home for the Diwali holidays. Her father, Rajesh Singh, is a lawyer practising in Lucknow. See pictures of the accident... How the accident unfolded Lawyer Rajesh Singh lives in Vrindavan, under the jurisdiction of the PGI police station. His family includes his wife, Geeta, and daughter, Sameeksha. On Thursday (19 Nov) night, Geeta and Sameeksha went to attend a wedding at Shivgarh Resort in Mohanlalganj with their neighbours Shikhar, his wife Sukriti and his mother, Asha. At around 11.45 pm, the group was returning home by car. Near Harikanshgarhi, Shikhar, who was driving, suddenly spotted a dumper ahead and lost control of the car. The vehicle became trapped between the dumper and a truck, leaving it badly damaged. Police and locals launch rescue operation After receiving information about the accident, Harikanshgarhi outpost in-charge Shiv Kumar and constable Rahul Kumar Rana reached the spot. With the help of local residents, they rescued Shikhar, Sukriti, Asha and Geeta and shifted them to Trauma Centre-2. Rescuers took around one and a half hours to free Sameeksha, who was trapped in the rear of the car. She was rushed to Trauma Centre-2 in critical condition, but doctors declared her dead. The four injured occupants are undergoing treatment at the hospital. Risk of CNG cylinder explosion during rescue The car was powered by CNG, raising concerns about a possible explosion during the rescue operation. After Sameeksha was pulled out, the cylinder was removed from the vehicle as a precaution. Dumper driver flees, truck taken into police custody The dumper driver fled the scene after the accident, while police seized the truck involved in the crash. Sameeksha's body has been kept in the trauma centre's mortuary. Police said further action would be taken after receiving a complaint from the family. Residents said heavy vehicles leave the plant in the wrong direction After the accident, local residents raised questions about the arrangements at the UltraTech aggregate plant. They alleged that trucks and dumpers often leave the plant at high speed in the wrong direction onto the highway, while loaded vehicles travel against the flow of traffic. According to residents, the movement of heavy vehicles outside the plant raises clouds of dust, making it difficult for drivers travelling along the highway to see the road ahead clearly. As a result, there is always a risk of an accident.

stories.title: Rain alert issued for 41 Purvanchal districts:UP records season's coldest night, dense fog in 28 districts; Cyclone Akvan impact
stories.summary: The impact of Cyclone Akvan, which has formed over the Bay of Bengal, is now being felt in Uttar Pradesh. An alert has been issued for rain and lightning in 41 districts of Purvanchal over the next 24 hours. Dense fog covered 28 cities on Friday morning, including Gorakhpur, Kushinagar, Deoria, Jaunpur, Muzaffarnagar and Sambhal. Visibility dropped so sharply that it was difficult to see beyond 10 metres. Night temperatures in the state have fallen below 10°C. Kanpur was the coldest city of the season, recording a minimum temperature of 9.4°C. The night temperature in Hardoi and Muzaffarnagar also dropped to 10°C. Meanwhile, Bahraich and Chandauli recorded the highest daytime temperature of 29°C. Atul Kumar Singh, a meteorologist in Lucknow, said, The impact of Cyclone Akvan has increased cloud movement across the state. Rain is likely in eastern UP on November 21 and 22. Severe cold, biting chill and fog are expected to intensify afterwards. Weather pictures Night temperatures in Uttar Pradesh fell below 10 degrees Day temperatures in Uttar Pradesh fell below 30 degrees Farmers advised to take precautions while sowing and irrigating rabi crops With rain likely in November, farmers have been advised to remain cautious while managing rabi crops. In particular, those sowing wheat, gram, peas and mustard in Purvanchal should ensure proper drainage in their fields. Waterlogging in low-lying fields can damage crops. Farmers should avoid unnecessary irrigation in fields that already have sufficient moisture due to rainfall. Decisions on sowing and irrigation should be based on weather conditions and soil moisture. Take care of these crops amid cold and fog

stories.title: Fake medicine racket busted in Varanasi:Mastermind feared for his life, said he would quit operations in UP before arrest
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force (STF) has uncovered a major counterfeit medicine manufacturing unit in Himachal Pradesh following an investigation initiated by the Varanasi drug department. The STF carried out the raid with a team of 10 drug inspectors from Uttar Pradesh. The investigation began after Varanasi Drug Inspector Junab Ali lodged a complaint. To track down the alleged mastermind, Abhishek Kumar, the STF and drug department team travelled to Mohania in Bihar. However, his mobile phone was switched off there. Before his arrest, Abhishek reportedly spoke to someone and said, "We will not operate in Uttar Pradesh anymore, otherwise we will be killed." The STF later laid a trap and arrested him from Varanasi. Investigation exposes counterfeit medicine network The probe subsequently uncovered links to a syndicate operating in Saharanpur and led investigators to a counterfeit medicine factory in Solan, Himachal Pradesh. To establish whether the counterfeit medicines were being supplied for sale in Varanasi or Bihar, Dainik Bhaskar spoke to Drug Inspector Junab Ali. The report also examines how the medicines were being counterfeited and how investigators managed to dismantle the network. Read the full report… Criminals arrested after supplying counterfeit medicines in Varanasi Drug Inspector Junaab Ali said, “We had been receiving complaints about counterfeit medicines being sold in Varanasi for several days. During the investigation, we found the medicines at a medical shop in Jansa.” He also said, “There were two or three strips of Nurokind-LC tablets. This led us to Surendra Nath, who named Abhishek as the mastermind.” He added, “We obtained details of their transactions through the Jangi app and other sources. After tracing and arresting Abhishek, we uncovered the entire operation. He told us that the medicines were never supposed to be supplied in Varanasi. That is why we were caught.” Surendra Nath acted as Abhishek's courier, says drug inspector Junab Ali said, “Surendra Nath, who was arrested in Varanasi, works as a medical representative. On the second floor of his house in Parmanandpur, we recovered fake medicines, including some strips of Nurokind-LC and Zerodol-SP.” He added, “During questioning, he said he did not know that Abhishek, a resident of Duddhi in Sonbhadra, was sending him the packets. He was supposed to place them in vehicles travelling to Bihar. Several boxes delivered to him were often found torn open. Abhishek had instructed him to destroy the medicines in such boxes.” He further said, “However, driven by greed, Surendra began selling the medicines at low prices without bills to medical stores in rural areas of Varanasi.” ‘We must stop operating in UP or they will kill us’ Junab Ali said, "We lodged a written complaint at Rohnia police station on 4 November, when Surendra Nath was arrested. With the help of the police, we then traced Abhishek and tracked his location to Mohania in Bihar. “We followed him to Mohania, but could not catch him. He switched off his mobile phone and later activated a new number, which we managed to trace. During the surveillance, a call recording captured him saying, ‘I must not work in Uttar Pradesh anymore. Otherwise, they will kill me there.’” Haseen from Saharanpur supplied counterfeit medicines During questioning, Abhishek revealed several key details about the network. Drug Inspector Junab Ali said, "Abhishek was in contact with Haseen, a resident of Saharanpur. Haseen procured medicines from Himachal Pradesh and couriered them to Abhishek for supply in Bihar. “In Varanasi, Surendra Nath sold the medicines to him out of greed, following which the drug department caught him. The STF later arrested Haseen in Saharanpur. Based on the information he provided, the team conducted a major operation in Solan, Himachal Pradesh, where a counterfeit medicine factory was uncovered. Fake medicines were allegedly being supplied from there to various parts of the country.” Now, find out how these medicines are fake... Suspicious labelling exposed counterfeit medicines Drug Inspector Junab Ali said counterfeit medicines could be identified through irregularities in their composition and errors in labelling. The packaging of the Nurokind-LC and Zerodol-SP tablets recovered during the investigation had been copied, but the labels contained several mistakes. He said the packaging designs used by reputed pharmaceutical companies had been replicated with errors that established manufacturers would not normally make. Several letters that should have appeared in lower case were printed in capital letters, raising suspicion about the medicines. Laboratory tests later confirmed that the tablets did not contain the required active ingredients. Zerodol-SP tablets lacked key pain-relieving ingredient Explaining the findings, Junab Ali said Zerodol-SP is a painkiller but the counterfeit tablets did not contain aceclofenac, its active pain-relieving ingredient. As a result, patients continued taking the medicine without getting any relief. He denied that the consignment was meant for supply in Varanasi, saying it was intended for Bihar. However, driven by greed, Surendra Nath allegedly began selling medicines from damaged boxes in rural areas of Varanasi. He supplied them to medical stores in small quantities of four or five strips. Public urged to demand bills when buying medicines Appealing to people to remain alert against counterfeit medicines, Drug Inspector Junab Ali said, “People must avoid buying fake medicines. Whenever they purchase medicines, they should ask the medical store for a proper bill. They should never buy medicines without a bill. This is the most effective way to prevent the sale of counterfeit medicines.” What are Nurokind-LC and Zerodol-SP tablets used for? Nurokind-LC tablets are primarily used to address deficiencies of nutrients such as vitamin B12, folic acid and carnitine in the body. They are also prescribed to help manage nerve weakness and treat anaemia, a condition caused by a deficiency of red blood cells or haemoglobin. The three main active ingredients in Nurokind-LC Tablet • Levocarnitine (500 mg): Helps produce energy in the body and supports the better functioning of the nerves and muscles. • Methylcobalamin (1,500 mcg): The active form of vitamin B12, which supports the production of red blood cells and the repair of nerves. • Folic acid (1.5 mg): Supports the production of healthy blood cells, cell growth and nerve health. Zerodol-SP Tablet is mainly used to relieve pain, swelling and inflammation in the body. It is a prescription medicine. Zerodol-SP tablets primarily contain three active ingredients • Aceclofenac: An NSAID painkiller that reduces the chemicals responsible for pain and inflammation. • Paracetamol: A medicine that relieves pain and reduces fever. • Serratiopeptidase: An enzyme that helps reduce inflammation by breaking down proteins associated with inflammation.

stories.title: CM Yogi takes selfies with students during tablet distribution:Ravi Kishan says devices are for studying, not watching films
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath distributed tablets to students in Gorakhpur on Friday. He interacted with them about their studies and also took selfies with students from the stage at an event held at Champa Devi Park. Yogi said the tablets were not merely devices for watching reels but tools to support education. “In the first phase, 60 lakh young people were given tablets and smartphones. Later, students requested tablets instead of smartphones. In the second phase, we are going to distribute 25 lakh tablets. After Lucknow, Gorakhpur is hosting the second programme,” he said. See pictures… Yogi takes a dig at Ravi Kishan During the event, Yogi also made a light-hearted remark about Gorakhpur MP and actor Ravi Kishan. “I thought the young people would arrive by 10 am, but wondered whether Ravi Kishan had woken up yet. I was told he was getting ready, so I asked him to hurry up. I thought he would sing one or two songs here, but he left the song unfinished,” the Chief Minister said. Addressing the gathering, Ravi Kishan said, “These tablets are not for watching films but for studying.” Yogi says tablet scheme has reached 3 crore people The Chief Minister said a study conducted by IIM Lucknow after the first phase of tablet distribution found that the scheme had benefited around 3 crore people. According to the study, 46% of families had seen a digital device for the first time. These families could not afford to buy tablets or smartphones on their own. The study also found that access to these devices had a positive impact on students’ learning abilities.

stories.summary: To manage the rush of passengers after the Chhath festival, the Railways has decided to operate eight special trains from Gorakhpur. These include services connecting Chhapra with Anand Vihar Terminal, Gorakhpur with Delhi, Hadapsar (Pune), Valsad and Udhna, and Chhapra with Lokmanya Tilak Terminus and Anand Vihar. The trains will operate on different dates between November 20 and 26. They are expected to provide relief to passengers travelling towards Delhi, Mumbai, Pune and Gujarat. While some trains will make a single trip, others will operate two trips. The Railways has also announced their schedules and coach compositions. Special train between Gorakhpur and Delhi on November 21 Train 05019, the Gorakhpur-Delhi Festival Special, will depart from Gorakhpur at 2.40 pm on November 21. It will travel via Khalilabad, Basti, Gonda, Burhwal, Lucknow and Kanpur Central, reaching Delhi at 8.20 am the next day. On the return journey, train 05020, the Delhi-Gorakhpur Special, will depart from Delhi at 11.10 am on November 22. It will pass through Ghaziabad, Tundla, Kanpur, Lucknow, Burhwal, Gonda, Basti and Khalilabad, reaching Gorakhpur at 5.05 am the next day. The train will have 15 coaches, including six sleeper-class coaches, seven general second-class coaches and two SLRD coaches. Chhapra-Anand Vihar train to run on November 21 Train 05013, the Chhapra-Anand Vihar Terminal Special, will depart from Chhapra at 5 pm on November 21. It will travel via Siwan, Thawe, Tamkuhi Road, Padrauna, Ramkola and Kaptanganj, reaching Gorakhpur at 10.40 pm. From there, it will continue via Khalilabad, Basti, Gonda, Burhwal, Lucknow, Kanpur and Tundla, reaching Anand Vihar at 3.50 pm the next day. On the return journey, train 05014 will depart from Anand Vihar at 6.45 pm on November 22. It will reach Gorakhpur at 12.55 pm the next day and continue via Kaptanganj, Ramkola, Padrauna, Tamkuhi Road, Thawe and Siwan, reaching Chhapra at 6.40 pm. The train will have 18 coaches. Gorakhpur-Pune special train on November 21 Train 05011, the Gorakhpur-Hadapsar (Pune) Special, will operate for one trip on November 21. It will depart from Gorakhpur at 9.55 pm. The train will travel via Basti, Mankapur, Gonda, Lucknow, Kanpur, Orai and Jhansi. It will then pass through Bina, Bhopal, Itarsi, Khandwa, Bhusaval and Manmad. After that, it will travel via Kopargaon, Belapur, Ahilyanagar and the Daund chord line, reaching Hadapsar at 7.30 am on the third day. The train will have 20 coaches, including four sleeper-class coaches, 14 general second-class coaches and two SLRD coaches. Gorakhpur-Valsad special train on November 20 Train 05061, the Gorakhpur-Valsad Reserved Special, will depart from Gorakhpur at 2.35 pm on November 20. It will travel via Basti, Gonda, Barabanki, Badshahnagar, Aishbagh and Kanpur Central. It will then pass through Agra, Bayana, Gangapur City, Kota, Ratlam and Vadodara, reaching Valsad at 7.35 pm the next day. On the return journey, train 05062 will depart from Valsad at 10.10 pm on November 21. It will travel via Surat, Vadodara, Ratlam, Kota, Agra, Kanpur, Aishbagh, Barabanki and Gonda, reaching Gorakhpur at 5.20 am on the third day. The train will have 15 coaches, including a generator-cum-luggage van, general chair car, air-conditioned chair car, sleeper and AC third-class coaches. Chhapra-Mumbai special train on November 20 Train 05117, the Chhapra-Lokmanya Tilak Terminus Reserved Special, will depart from Chhapra at 8 pm on November 20. It will travel via Mashrakh, Dighwa Dubauli, Gopalganj, Thawe, Tamkuhi Road, Padrauna, Ramkola and Kaptanganj, reaching Gorakhpur at 2.35 am the next day. From there, it will continue via Khalilabad, Basti, Gonda, Gomti Nagar, Aishbagh, Kanpur and Jhansi, reaching Lokmanya Tilak Terminus at 12.10 pm on the third day. On the return journey, train 05118, the Lokmanya Tilak Terminus-Thawe Special, will depart at 2.40 pm on November 22. It will reach Gorakhpur at 10.55 pm the next day. From Gorakhpur, it will travel via Pipraich, Kaptanganj, Ramkola, Padrauna and Tamkuhi Road, reaching Thawe at 2.45 am on the third day. The train will have 20 coaches, including nine sleeper-class coaches, nine general second-class coaches and two SLRD coaches. Unreserved Chhapra-Anand Vihar train to make two trips Train 05057, the Chhapra-Anand Vihar Unreserved Special, will depart from Chhapra at 9 pm on November 22 and 25. It will travel via Siwan, Thawe, Tamkuhi Road, Padrauna, Ramkola and Kaptanganj, reaching Gorakhpur at 2.40 am the next day. From there, it will pass through Khalilabad, Basti, Gonda, Burhwal, Sitapur, Shahjahanpur, Bareilly and Moradabad, reaching Anand Vihar at 4.55 pm. On the return journey, train 05058 will depart from Anand Vihar at 8.10 pm on November 23 and 26. It will reach Gorakhpur at 10.30 am the next day and continue via Kaptanganj, Ramkola, Padrauna, Tamkuhi Road, Thawe and Siwan, reaching Chhapra at 4.10 pm. The train will have 20 coaches, including 18 general second-class coaches and two SLRD coaches. Gorakhpur-Udhna special train on November 22 Train 05017, the Gorakhpur-Udhna Reserved Special, will depart from Gorakhpur at 7.35 am on November 22. It will travel via Khalilabad, Basti, Gonda, Barabanki, Badshahnagar, Aishbagh and Kanpur Central. It will then pass through Agra, Bayana, Gangapur City, Kota, Ratlam and Vadodara, reaching Udhna at 11.50 am the next day. On the return journey, train 05018 will depart from Udhna at 3 pm on November 23. It will travel via Surat, Vadodara, Ratlam, Kota, Agra, Kanpur, Aishbagh, Barabanki, Gonda and Basti, reaching Gorakhpur at 8.30 pm. The train will have 18 coaches, including general, sleeper, AC third-class and AC second-class coaches.

stories.title: 7 killed, including groom's four friends:Car travelling at 100 kmph hits bike, then tree; group was heading from UP to Bihar
stories.summary: A car carrying wedding guests from Uttar Pradesh rammed into a motorcycle at a speed of around 100 kmph in Bihar. The car then reportedly flew nearly 20 feet into the air, overturned five to six times and crashed into a tree. Seven people, including four friends of the groom, were killed in the accident. The victims included four car occupants and three motorcycle riders. Five young men from Bhatoura village in Uttar Pradesh’s Ghazipur district were travelling to Bihar to attend a wedding. One of the motorcycle riders was also from Ghazipur and had come to visit his maternal uncle. The accident took place on Thursday night in the Rajpur police station area of Buxar district. Hearing screams, local residents rushed to the spot and broke open the car doors to rescue those trapped inside. Three car occupants died on the spot, while four others succumbed to their injuries during treatment. The deceased car occupants were identified as Badal Kumar (30), Irfan Ansari (25), Arbaaz Ali (20) and Divyanshu Thakur (22), all residents of Bhatoura village in Ghazipur. The three motorcycle riders who died were Arun Kumar (22), a resident of Uttaroli village in Ghazipur, and Shubham Kumar (21) and Shivam Kumar (18), both from Buxar district. Bhatoura village head Ajit Singh said the car was being driven by Chhangur Kumar alias Satendra (25), also from the village. His whereabouts have been unknown since the accident. He had bought a second-hand Hyundai i20 car just two months ago. One rider’s leg severed; car badly damaged Five young men from Bhatoura village, under the jurisdiction of the Gahmar police station in Ghazipur, were travelling to Bihar. They were going to attend a wedding in Bishunpura village in Ramgarh, Kaimur district. Meanwhile, three young men from Sonpa village had just travelled around 50 metres from their home on a motorcycle on National Highway 319A when the car carrying the wedding guests hit them from behind. The impact was so severe that Arun, who was riding pillion, lost his left leg. It was severed and thrown some distance away. The car was also badly damaged. ‘The car was speeding and the driver lost control’ Eyewitness Raviranjan Singh said the car was travelling at more than 100 kmph. The driver could not control the vehicle despite seeing the motorcycle. After hitting the bike, the car went out of control, became airborne, overturned several times and crossed a water-filled pit about 10 feet deep beside the road before crashing into a tree. Arun was preparing for Army recruitment Arun Kumar (22), a resident of Uttaroli village in Ghazipur, was the younger of two brothers. He was preparing for recruitment into the Army. He had arrived a day earlier to visit his maternal uncle, Heraram Rajbhar, in Sonpa village. On Thursday evening, he was riding towards Mahavir Sthan with his cousins’ local friends, Shubham Kumar (21) from Saura village and Shivam Kumar (18) from Sikraul, when the accident occurred. Eyewitnesses describe the impact Rajesh Rai, an eyewitness and president of the Jalilpur PACS, said the sound of the collision was so loud that it left him shaken. “When I turned around, I heard screams coming from the car. I rushed to the spot with other local residents and saw all three motorcycle riders lying on the road and struggling in pain,” he said.

stories.title: UP STF kills shooter Naseem Durrani in encounter:Wanted in Delhi minister Kapil Mishra's office murder case
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force (STF) killed shooter Naseem Durrani (37) in an encounter in Bulandshahr. A reward of ₹50,000 had been announced for his arrest. He was wanted in connection with the murder of a man outside Delhi minister Kapil Mishra's office four days ago. The STF and Delhi Police had received information that Durrani was hiding in Bulandshahr and planning to flee. When the teams surrounded him, he opened fire. Around 15 to 20 rounds were fired from both sides. Durrani was killed in the retaliatory firing after being hit by two bullets in the chest. The encounter took place at around 1 am on Thursday in the Sikandrabad police station area. Durrani, a resident of Delhi, had 26 criminal cases against him, including four murder cases. He was also in contact with underworld don Chhota Shakeel. In 2017, Shakeel had allegedly given him a contract to kill Chhota Rajan, who was lodged in Tihar Jail at the time. Durrani was also accused of conspiring to murder Pakistani-origin writer Tarek Fatah. Opened fire fearing arrest; killed in retaliatory firing Noida STF Additional SP Rajkumar Mishra said Durrani was escaping on a motorcycle. When the team surrounded him, he opened fire at the police, fearing arrest. He was hit by a bullet in the retaliatory firing and fell to the ground. He was rushed to a hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Police recovered a motorcycle and two .32-bore pistols from the spot. Three pictures of encounter… Three major crimes linked to Durrani 1. Killed a man in Delhi four days ago On November 16, Durrani shot dead a man named Sameer in Sonia Vihar, under the Khajuri Khas police station area of Delhi. He fled after the incident. During the investigation, police examined CCTV footage from the surrounding area, while crime and forensic science laboratory (FSL) teams collected evidence from the spot. Durrani emerged as the main accused, following which Delhi Police launched a search for him. 2. Killed another man in May 2026 On May 26, 2026, a shooting took place in Delhi's Khajuri Khas area. A man named Raja Mewati was shot. Police took him to JPC Hospital, where doctors declared him dead. During the investigation, Durrani, also known as Rizwan, was identified as the main shooter in the murder. 3. Shot at a woman in Ghaziabad a year ago Additional SP Rajkumar Mishra said Durrani had opened fire at a woman in Loni, Ghaziabad, in 2025. She was injured but survived after receiving treatment. Ghaziabad Police had announced a reward of ₹50,000 for information leading to his arrest in this case. Durrani was married and had three sisters Naseem, also known as Rizwan, was the son of Islamuddin, alias Budhu. He originally belonged to Rajiv Gandhi Nagar in New Mustafabad, Delhi. His family included his father Islamuddin, mother Nafisa, wife Zeba and three sisters — Rubina, Rani and Zeenat. According to police, Durrani had been involved in criminal cases since 2010. More than 22 cases were registered against him in Delhi and Uttar Pradesh, including murder, robbery, dacoity, Arms Act violations and attacks on police personnel. Second encounter in UP in three days Two days before Durrani was killed, contract killer Wahid Ansari (35) was killed in an encounter in Ambedkar Nagar. He was allegedly a major arms supplier in eastern Uttar Pradesh and carried out murders for money. Police surrounded him on Tuesday night, following which he opened fire. He was hit by four bullets in the chest and leg and fell on the road. Two police personnel were injured in the encounter. SP Prachi Singh narrowly escaped after a bullet hit her bulletproof jacket. 259 criminals killed in encounters in eight years According to the state government, UP Police killed 266 criminals in encounters between March 2017 and October 2025. During this period, more than 16,000 police encounters took place. Over 31,000 criminals were arrested, while more than 10,000 were shot and injured.

stories.title: Daughter asked, ‘What would I say if I got lost?’:Father demands accused nephew be burnt alive; 4-year-old girl was raped murdered
stories.summary: A father in Uttar Pradesh’s Hardoi has demanded the death penalty for his 20-year-old nephew, who allegedly raped and murdered his four-year-old daughter. He said the accused should either be killed in a police encounter or burnt alive in front of the family. “The man who killed my daughter should be killed in an encounter. Otherwise, pour petrol over him and burn him alive in front of us. He should be made to suffer before being killed so that no such monster emerges in the area again. What happened to us today could happen to another family tomorrow. He must not be allowed to remain alive,” the grieving father said. The girl went missing from outside her home on 13 November. Her body was found in an orchard on 15 November, around 2 km from the village. The accused, identified as Rizbi Yadav, was the girl's cousin uncle. He had joined the family in searching for her and even dug the pit for her burial. A Dainik Bhaskar team travelled 37 km from the district headquarters and spoke to the family to piece together the sequence of events. First, know what happened... A four-year-old girl went missing from outside her home in a village under Lonar Kotwali police station on 13 November. Her family searched for her throughout the day but failed to find her. They subsequently lodged a missing-person complaint at the police station that night. Teams from the Special Operations Group (SOG), surveillance unit and dog squad, along with police personnel from six police stations, were deployed to trace the child. On the evening of 15 November, her body was found in bushes in an orchard around 2 km from the village. There was a cut mark on her neck, and rape was suspected. The incident triggered anger in the village. During the investigation, police identified the girl's cousin uncle, Rizbi Yadav, as the accused. He allegedly raped her and killed her to prevent her from disclosing the crime. Police arrested him on 18 November and sent him to jail. Now read what the father said... The girl's father, who works as a Provincial Armed Constabulary (PRD) personnel, said he also works in farming in the village. He has three daughters and two brothers. “On 13 November, before leaving for the fields in the morning, I ate a rasgulla and gave some to both my daughters. I saw the girl playing once in the afternoon. In the evening, I received a call at home saying she was missing,” he said. My cousin searched for her everywhere with us The father said the family searched throughout the village and also took his father to the police outpost. Police teams immediately joined the search and continued looking for the girl through the night. He said the accused also pretended to help them find her. “He went with me and my paternal uncle's sons to search for her as far as Bareilly, Turia and Bawan. He did not speak much to anyone, so we never suspected him,” the father said. Family did not suspect him The father said the accused appeared equally distressed after the girl went missing. “Everyone in the family was dejected, and he also looked sad. We thought he was grieving as a family member. We had no idea that he was stabbing us in the back,” he said. He added that after the girl's funeral, the Circle Officer (CO) and a police team in plain clothes took the accused away. The police have not yet brought him face to face with the family. Daughter often asked what she should do if she got lost The father recalled that his daughter would often ask him, “Dad, what will I say if I get lost somewhere?” “She would then answer innocently, ‘I will tell them my father's name and my grandfather's name. Then someone will bring me back and drop me in my village’,” he said. He added that the family had lost their newborn son just a month and a half earlier and was still coping with that grief when the girl was killed. “My wife is in a very bad condition. She has to take medicines every day. Our only demand is that this monster should be burnt alive after being doused in petrol, or the police should kill him in an encounter,” he said. Mother is distraught since girl's death The girl's mother has been inconsolable since her daughter's death and reportedly loses consciousness several times while speaking about the incident. She said the accused should be made to suffer even more than her daughter did before being killed. Only then, she said, would her daughter's soul and her own find peace. “On the morning of the incident, my daughter told me, ‘Mummy, I am going out to play.’ I gave her some tea before she left. In the afternoon, I called out to her, but she was nowhere to be found,” the mother said. She described her daughter as cheerful and playful. Recalling the Diwali celebrations, she said the child had burst several firecrackers and the family had never imagined that such a tragedy would strike. “My only demand is that the person who did this should be tortured to death,” she said. Grandfather demands that accused be shot The girl's grandfather said he was on duty in Sandila when the incident took place. “He has committed such a despicable act against our family and must be punished.” He added, “If he is spared today because he is considered a family member, he could target another child tomorrow. Just shoot him. We have nothing to do with him, whether he is a relative, a villager or anyone else.” Accused misled family even after murder The grandfather alleged that Rizbi continued to mislead the family after killing the girl and accompanied them to the police outpost. “He searched for her everywhere with us but never told us anything about the place where he had committed the crime. When my sons saw the body, they screamed,” he said. The grandfather further alleged that the accused dug the pit himself and took part in the last rites. He also accompanied the police when the inspector called him. “He stood there calmly. Our only demand is that he should be hanged,” the grandfather said. Both parents of accused are dead Rizbi Yadav, 20, has lost both his parents and is the eldest of four brothers. All four brothers live in Delhi, where Rizbi works in the water supply sector. His house in the village is close to the girl's home. He had returned to the village for Diwali. According to the account of the incident, Rizbi saw the girl playing alone on the afternoon of 13 November and took her to a field on the pretext of feeding her. He allegedly raped her there. Fearing that she would tell her family about the assault, he strangled her and left her body in the field before returning home. Father named him after a constable Villagers said Rizbi's father had frequently faced police action over disputes and had been jailed several times. A constable named Rizbi would arrest him and take him away. His father reportedly liked the constable's name so much that he named his son after him. Police confirm arrest Harpalpur CO Praveen Kumar Yadav said a missing-person report was registered on 13 November and the girl's body was recovered during the search. “The post-mortem confirmed rape. The investigation revealed that her cousin uncle, Rizbi Yadav, was responsible for the murder. He has been arrested and sent to jail,” he said.

stories.title: Woman arrives at boyfriend's house with wedding procession:Says, 'We were together for 7 years, but he is now marrying someone else'
stories.summary: A woman from Dehradun arrived at her boyfriend's house in Shamli with her mother and family members, accompanied by a wedding procession with drums and music. She was carrying a banner that read, 'I have brought a wedding procession to take the bride home'. The woman alleged that her boyfriend had been in a relationship with her for seven years and repeatedly promised to marry her. However, he is now set to marry another woman on November 21. Her unexpected arrival with the procession drew a crowd outside her boyfriend's house. The incident took place at around 6 pm on Thursday in the Elam town area under Kandhla police station limits. First, see two pictures.... Here is the full story… Sonia, who lives in Dehradun, is a BSc student. Her boyfriend, Ankush, serves in the Merchant Navy and lives in Elam town in Shamli. The two had stopped communicating over the past few days. During this time, Sonia learnt that Ankush's marriage had been arranged with another woman and that he was due to get married two days later. She was distressed after learning about his upcoming marriage. They met at a wedding seven years ago Sonia said she first met Ankush in 2019 at his sister's wedding. They initially became friends, but their friendship gradually developed into a relationship. They continued talking and meeting, while Ankush repeatedly promised to marry her. He had also created a wedding invitation card with her and sent it to her on WhatsApp, she claimed. Allegedly behaved inappropriately with her on the pretext of introducing her to his sister Sonia alleged that Ankush once took her along in Dehradun on the pretext of introducing her to his sister and a friend. She claimed that he took her to another room and behaved inappropriately with her. He continued promising to marry her during this period, she alleged. According to Sonia, Ankush's family members were also aware of their relationship. Learnt about his wedding after finding out about the invitation Sonia said she recently learnt that Ankush's marriage had been arranged with another woman and that his wedding procession was scheduled for November 21. She tried contacting him but received no response. She then informed her family about the entire matter. After this, she travelled to Elam with nine family members, including her mother and sister. "I have come here to make him fulfil the promise of marriage he made to me. I remained in this relationship for so many years because I trusted him. The entire incident has caused me mental distress, and my health has also suffered. I will marry Ankush," she said. Crowd gathers outside boyfriend's house as procession arrives When Sonia and her family reached Ankush's house carrying the banner, a crowd gathered in the neighbourhood. A team from the Elam police outpost reached the spot after receiving information about the incident. However, Sonia and her family were not satisfied with the police's initial response. They returned to Ankush's house and demanded strict action. ASP Sumit Shukla said police personnel were sent to the spot after receiving information. The police are gathering details about the matter, and further action will be taken after an investigation.

stories.title: Agra student drowns in Ganga in Rishikesh:Was bathing in river with friends; 32 students had arrived on a school trip
stories.summary: A 15-year-old student from Agra was swept away by the strong current of the Ganga while bathing in the river in the Laxman Jhula area of Rishikesh. He had visited the town on an excursion with 32 other students and five teachers from his school. The student was bathing with his companions at a ghat when the strong current swept him away. His fellow students raised an alarm after witnessing the incident. Search operation launched, student remains missing Following the incident, the water police, local residents and the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) launched a search operation. However, the student remained missing until late evening. PHOTOS from the rescue operation... Class 10 student swept away while bathing with friends Ansh (15), a Class 10 student and son of Rajkumar Sharma, a resident of Rohta in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, had arrived in Rishikesh on an excursion on Thursday (19 Nov). His group reached a ghat near the Laxman Jhula bridge, where Ansh went to bathe in the Ganga with other students. He was swept away by the river's strong current. Water police and locals attempt rescue After Ansh was swept away, the students accompanying him raised an alarm. Hearing their cries, water police personnel and local residents at the spot attempted to rescue him. However, the strong current carried him further downstream. On receiving information about the incident, an SDRF rescue team from the Dhalwala post reached the spot. Deep divers were deployed to search for the missing student. Search operation suspended after dark The SDRF team conducted an extensive search in the Ganga but could not locate Ansh. The operation was temporarily suspended after dark as it became difficult to continue the search at night. The search will resume on Friday. Laxmanjhula police informed the student's family about the incident. Teams from the Laxmanjhula police station and the water police remained at the site.
